<script>
    function openAccountsDDL() {
        let ddl = document.querySelector("#account__dropdown-items ul");
        let btn = document.querySelector("#account-dropdown-btn");

        if (ddl) {
            const isOpen = ddl.style.display === "block";
            ddl.style.display = isOpen ? "none" : "block";

            if (btn) {
                btn.setAttribute("aria-expanded", String(!isOpen));
            }

            if (!isOpen) {
                trapFocus(ddl, btn);
            } else {
                releaseFocus();
            }
        }
    }

    function trapFocus(container, triggerBtn) {
        const focusableSelectors = 'a[href], button:not([disabled]), input, select, textarea, [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])';
        const focusableElements = container.querySelectorAll(focusableSelectors);
        const first = focusableElements[0];
        const last = focusableElements[focusableElements.length - 1];

        if (first) first.focus();

        function handleKeyDown(e) {
            if (e.key === 'Escape') {
                openAccountsDDL();
                triggerBtn.focus();
                return;
            }

            if (e.key === 'Tab') {
                if (e.shiftKey) {
                    if (document.activeElement === first) {
                        e.preventDefault();
                        last.focus();
                    }
                } else {
                    if (document.activeElement === last) {
                        e.preventDefault();
                        first.focus();
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        document.addEventListener('keydown', handleKeyDown);

        document._accountMenuHandler = handleKeyDown;
    }

    function releaseFocus() {
        if (document._accountMenuHandler) {
            document.removeEventListener('keydown', document._accountMenuHandler);
            document._accountMenuHandler = null;
        }
    }
</script>

            <div class="image-widget__text-container">
                    <h3 class="image-widget__text-container__title">
                        What is Microgeneration and Feed-in Tariffs?
                    </h3>
                    <svg class="icon rectangle-thin">
                        <use xlink:href="#icon-rectangle-thin"></use>
                    </svg>
                    <div class="image-widget__text-container__content">
                        <p><a href="/about-energia/latest-news/microgeneration">Microgeneration</a>  is when you generate your own electricity using technologies such as <a href="/home-upgrades/solar-energy">solar PV panels</a> or solar battery storage. During the day, your solar panels generate electricity that can be used in your home or business. If you generate more electricity than you use, the excess energy is automatically exported back to the electricity grid. The payment you receive for exporting this surplus electricity is commonly known as a feed-in tariff. In Ireland, this payment is officially provided through the Clean Export Guarantee (CEG).</p><p><br></p>
                    </div>

                        <p>Energia currently offers a microgeneration rate of  <span data-olk-copy-source="MessageBody">18.5 </span>cent (18.5c/kWh).                     </h3>
                    <svg class="icon rectangle-thin">

                    </svg>
                    <div class="image-widget__text-container__content">
                        <p>With Energia's Microgeneration Scheme, you'll receive a credit on your bi-monthly electricity bill for any excess renewable electricity you export to the grid. Thanks to your smart meter, readings are taken every 30 minutes and automatically sent to ESBN. </p><p>This exported energy is compensated through the Clean Export Guarantee (CEG) tariff, applied as a credit on your invoice rather than a direct bank transfer.         <h2 class="text-widget__text-container__header" style="text-align: center"><span style="color: rgba(60, 35, 115, 1); font-size: 30px">Who is Eligible?</span></h2><p>To join Energia’s Microgeneration Scheme, you must:</p><ul type="disc"><li>Own a microgenerator, such as a solar PV system</li><li>Have an export grid connection</li><li>Have a smart meter installed (Energia can request one for you)</li><li>Submit the NC6 form to ESBN (your installer may do this for you)<br> Eligible customers may also qualify for financial support via <a href="/home-upgrades/seai-grants">SEAI grants</a> to help offset installation costs. Once your export data is shared with Energia by ESBN, you'll begin receiving credits on your electricity bill.</li></ul><h2 class="text-widget__text-container__header" style="text-align: center"><span style="color: rgba(60, 35, 115, 1); font-size: 30px">How to Sign Up</span></h2><p>Here's how to sign up for Energia’s Microgeneration Scheme:</p><ul><li>Own a microgenerator (like solar PV) with an export grid connection.</li><li>Ensure your NC6 form is completed and submitted to ESBN. Your installer may have already done this.</li><li>Once ESBN processes your form, they notify Energia, and we’ll set up your export account.</li><li>Make sure both your electricity import and export are with Energia.</li><li>Once ESBN sends us your export data, you'll see payments as a credit on your Energia bill.</li></ul><h3><br><strong><span style="font-size: 18px">The Simple 4-Step Process</span></strong></h3><ol><li>1. Install solar panels or another microgenerator</li><li>2. Submit your NC6 form and install a smart meter</li><li>3. Start exporting surplus electricity to the grid</li><li>4. Receive credit on your Energia bill every 2 months</li></ol><h2 class="text-widget__text-container__header" style="text-align: center"><span style="color: rgba(60, 35, 115, 1); font-size: 30px">Benefits of Joining Energia’s Scheme</span></h2><ul type="disc"><li><strong>Payment for your surplus energy:</strong> Energia pays you for the excess electricity you export to the grid, currently at a rate of 18.5c per kWh.</li><li><strong>Contribute to a greener Ireland:</strong> Exporting your surplus green energy helps Ireland move towards a more sustainable future and reduces your carbon footprint.</li><li><strong>Potential tax exemptions:</strong> You may be eligible for a yearly tax exemption of €400 on income earned from selling excess electricity.</li><li><strong>Financial support:</strong> Grants from the <a href="https://www.seai.ie/">Sustainable Energy Authority of Ireland (SEAI)</a> can help cover installation costs.</li><li><strong>Smart Solar bundle:</strong> Energia offers a Smart Solar bundle that provides a saving of €750 on solar panel installation.</li><li><strong>No export cap:</strong> If you have a smart meter, there’s no limit to how much electricity you can export.</li></ul>
    </div>

We’re a trusted supplier of <a href="/about-energia/renewable-electricity">100% green energy</a>, committed to helping Ireland transition to a cleaner, more sustainable energy future.</p><p><span style="font-size: 14px">* total number of microgeneration customers as of April 2025</span></p>

                                    <div class="accordion__control__title">What is Microgeneration and the Microgeneration Scheme?</div>
                                    <div class="accordion__control__icon">
                                       <svg width="26" height="24" viewBox="0 0 26 24" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
                                        <path d="M12.667 0.5C19.4121 0.500166 24.833 5.67395 24.833 12C24.833 18.326 19.4121 23.4998 12.667 23.5C5.92171 23.5 0.5 18.3261 0.5 12C0.5 5.67385 5.92171 0.5 12.667 0.5Z" stroke="#AF195F"></path>

                            </h3>
                            <div id="accordionPanel-a549da93f803045448cc4be45f11275a4" class="accordion__panel" role="region" aria-labelledby="accordionControl-a549da93f803045448cc4be45f11275a4" hidden="">
                                <p>Microgeneration means producing your own renewable electricity, usually with solar panels (Solar PV). Energia’s <a href="https://www.energia.ie/home-upgrades/energia-and-the-microgeneration-scheme">Microgeneration Scheme</a> lets you earn money by sending any unused electricity back to the grid.</p>

<p><strong>Key points:</strong></p>

<ul>
	<li>You generate clean energy at home.</li>
	<li>Any extra electricity you don’t use can be exported to the grid.</li>
	<li>Energia pays you for the electricity you export under the scheme.</li>
</ul>

                            </div>
                            <h3 class="accordion__control__heading">
                                <button id="accordionControl-a8bb42b14498e4664972a64149a2d20c2" class="accordion__control" data-click-text="Am I eligible for the Microgeneration Scheme and the Clean Export Guarantee payment?" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="accordionPanel-a8bb42b14498e4664972a64149a2d20c2" data-accordion-control="" data-adobe-accordion-block="Collapsible Panel" data-adobe-accordion-title="Am I eligible for the Microgeneration Scheme and the Clean Export Guarantee payment?">
                                    <div class="accordion__control__title">Am I eligible for the Microgeneration Scheme and the Clean Export Guarantee payment?</div>
                                    <div class="accordion__control__icon">
                                       <svg width="26" height="24" viewBox="0 0 26 24" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
                                        <path d="M12.667 0.5C19.4121 0.500166 24.833 5.67395 24.833 12C24.833 18.326 19.4121 23.4998 12.667 23.5C5.92171 23.5 0.5 18.3261 0.5 12C0.5 5.67385 5.92171 0.5 12.667 0.5Z" stroke="#AF195F"></path>

                                        </svg>
                                    </div>
                                </button>
                            </h3>
                            <div id="accordionPanel-a8bb42b14498e4664972a64149a2d20c2" class="accordion__panel" role="region" aria-labelledby="accordionControl-a8bb42b14498e4664972a64149a2d20c2" hidden="">
                                <p>Yes, if you meet the following requirements:</p>

<p><strong>Eligibility checklist:</strong></p>

<ul>
	<li>You own a microgenerator, such as a <a href="https://www.energia.ie/home-upgrades/solar-energy">solar PV system</a>.</li>
	<li>You have an export grid connection.</li>
	<li>You have completed and submitted an NC6 form to <abbr title="Electricity Supply Board">ESB</abbr> Networks (your installer may have done this for you at the time of installation of the microgenerator.).</li>
</ul>

<p><br>
<strong>What happens next:</strong></p>

<ul>
	<li>Once <abbr title="Electricity Supply Board">ESB</abbr> Networks processes your NC6 form, they will notify Energia.</li>
	<li>We set up your export account and add payments to your electricity bill based on your export data.</li>
</ul>

<p><br>
<strong>Important for payment:</strong></p>

<ul>
	<li>If you don’t have a smart meter, you’ll need one installed by <abbr title="Electricity Supply Board">ESB</abbr> Networks to get paid for your exported electricity.</li>
	<li>You can<a href="https://www.esbnetworks.ie/services/manage-my-meter/about-smart-meters/smart-meter-form"> request a smart meter on the <abbr title="Electricity Supply Board">ESB</abbr> Networks website</a>.</li>
</ul>

                                <p>You’ll need a smart meter to join the Microgeneration Scheme and receive payments for exported electricity.</p>

<p><strong>What to do</strong></p>

<ul>
	<li>Request a smart meter installation from <abbr title="Electricity Supply Board">ESB</abbr> Networks.</li>
	<li>You can make the <a href="https://www.esbnetworks.ie/services/manage-my-meter/about-smart-meters/smart-meter-form">request directly on the <abbr title="Electricity Supply Board">ESB</abbr> Networks website</a>.</li>
</ul>

                                <p>Here’s how the process works and what you can do:</p>

<p><strong>How it works</strong></p>

<ul>
	<li><abbr title="Electricity Supply Board">ESB</abbr> Networks sends Energia a notification when your microgeneration installation is registered.</li>
	<li>We update your account and email you to confirm we’ve received this information.</li>
</ul>

<p> </p>

<ul>
	<li><strong>If you haven’t heard from us</strong></li>
	<li>Make sure your NC6 form and details were submitted correctly to <abbr title="Electricity Supply Board">ESB</abbr> Networks.</li>
	<li>If everything is complete and you still haven’t received confirmation, please contact Energia for assistance.</li>
</ul>

                                <p>No, not at the moment. To join the Microgeneration Scheme, your electricity import and export must be with the same supplier.</p>

                                <p>Deemed export is an estimated amount of electricity you export when you don’t have a smart meter. This method is less common now because smart meters provide accurate readings.</p>

<p><strong>Good to know</strong></p>

<ul>
	<li>Deemed export is only used if a smart meter isn’t installed.</li>
	<li>Smart meters give exact export data, so they’re the preferred option.</li>

                            </h3>
                            <div id="accordionPanel-a3930ee6a8bb24847932e3ebb45bef271" class="accordion__panel" role="region" aria-labelledby="accordionControl-a3930ee6a8bb24847932e3ebb45bef271" hidden="">
                                <p>The difference is in how your exported electricity is measured.</p>

<p><strong>Key differences</strong></p>

<ul>
	<li>Metered export uses real-time data from your smart meter, so it’s accurate.</li>
	<li>Deemed export is an estimated amount used when smart meter data isn’t available.</li>
</ul>

                            </div>

                                    <div class="accordion__control__icon">
                                       <svg width="26" height="24" viewBox="0 0 26 24" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">

                            <div id="accordionPanel-af425751b3e51452fbfb650a02a4a7a0e" class="accordion__panel" role="region" aria-labelledby="accordionControl-af425751b3e51452fbfb650a02a4a7a0e" hidden="">
                                <p>Your earnings depend on how much excess electricity you export to the grid. With Energia’s current rate of 18.5c per kWh, exporting 1,000 kWh in a year could earn you about €185 in credits.</p>

<p><strong>Good to know</strong></p>

<ul>
	<li>The more electricity you export, the more you earn.</li>
	<li>Payments are added as credits to your electricity bill.</li>
	<li>Check the <a href="/about-energia/our-tariffs">latest Energia rates</a> for up-to-date information.</li>
</ul>

                                <p>A feed-in tariff is the payment you receive for surplus electricity exported to the grid. Energia currently pays eligible customers 18.5c/kWh via the Clean Export Guarantee.</p>

Price Updates
Customer notice
We are increasing our residential Electricity and Gas prices from 12th October 2026.
Please see here for more information.
Energia Price update
What's changing?
From 12th October 2026, changes will apply to residential electricity and gas prices. Below you'll find a summary of the changes and what they mean for Energia customers.
Energia Price Changes
Electricity
customers will see a 4.73% increase to the average annual bill which equates to €1.67 per week. The electricity standing charge will increase by 5% for these customers.
Gas
customers will see a 9.38%
increase to the average annual bill which equates to €2.74 per week. There will be no change to gas standing charges.
Dual Fuel
customers will see a 6.73% increase to the average annual bill which equates to €4.41 per week.
The electricity standing charge will increase by 5% for these customers and there will be no change to gas standing charges.
Full details of changes to our individual rates and specific plans can be found at energia.ie/tariffs
Electricity % increase is based on the Estimated Annual Bill (EAB) for Energia’s Standard Electricity Plan and Energia's Smart Data Plan with typical annual electricity consumption of 4,200 kWh. Gas % increase is based on average annual gas consumption of 11,000 kWh. Inclusive of current Carbon Tax and updated PSO Levy effective 1
st
October 2026.
Why are prices changing?
We don’t take the decision to increase prices lightly and continue to look for ways to keep costs as low as possible for our customers.
However, continued volatility in global energy markets combined with increased network charges means we now need to make some changes to our electricity and gas prices, our first increase in gas since 2022. We fully understand that any changes to pricing affects households and encourage customers who are experiencing difficulties to engage with us for support.
Help, Support & Frequently Asked Questions
What can I do if I’m finding it hard to pay my bills?
If you’re having difficulty paying your bills, we’re here to help.
We collaborate with several charitable and support organisations such as St Vincent de Paul, MABS, Alone, and our customer service team are available to speak to any customers experiencing difficulty.
We have a range of options available for customers.
Please contact us if you have any worries about paying your bill.
How can I save on my electricity costs?
Make sure you are on the right plan for your home. You can check your usage using the Energia Insights app to understand where and when you are using the most energy in your home.
Some homes are better suited to Smart time of use tariffs while others will be more suited to 24 hour plans.
If you don’t think you are on the right tariff, talk to our team about changing to a different plan.
Will my rates change if I am in contract?
Yes. Our tariff rates are variable and are subject to change. This is included in our terms and conditions.
If you are currently on a discounted contract, your prices will be increasing from the 12th October 2026. However, your discount will remain the same and will be deducted from the standard rates applicable to your tariff.
As a result of these changes, you have a right to terminate your contract within the next 30 days. If you would like to discuss your plan, please call us to discuss the best option for you.
Will I be contacted directly about this price change?
We will be contacting customers directly by email to inform them of this change.
Faults & Emergencies
If you are having difficulty with your energy supply or smell gas please call us using our
fault and emergency contact numbers

<script>
    function openAccountsDDL() {
        let ddl = document.querySelector("#account__dropdown-items ul");
        let btn = document.querySelector("#account-dropdown-btn");

        if (ddl) {
            const isOpen = ddl.style.display === "block";
            ddl.style.display = isOpen ? "none" : "block";

            if (btn) {
                btn.setAttribute("aria-expanded", String(!isOpen));
            }

            if (!isOpen) {
                trapFocus(ddl, btn);
            } else {
                releaseFocus();
            }
        }
    }

    function trapFocus(container, triggerBtn) {
        const focusableSelectors = 'a[href], button:not([disabled]), input, select, textarea, [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])';
        const focusableElements = container.querySelectorAll(focusableSelectors);
        const first = focusableElements[0];
        const last = focusableElements[focusableElements.length - 1];

        if (first) first.focus();

        function handleKeyDown(e) {
            if (e.key === 'Escape') {
                openAccountsDDL();
                triggerBtn.focus();
                return;
            }

            if (e.key === 'Tab') {
                if (e.shiftKey) {
                    if (document.activeElement === first) {
                        e.preventDefault();
                        last.focus();
                    }
                } else {
                    if (document.activeElement === last) {
                        e.preventDefault();
                        first.focus();
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        document.addEventListener('keydown', handleKeyDown);

        document._accountMenuHandler = handleKeyDown;
    }

    function releaseFocus() {
        if (document._accountMenuHandler) {
            document.removeEventListener('keydown', document._accountMenuHandler);
            document._accountMenuHandler = null;
        }
    }
</script>

        <p><strong><span style="font-size: 30px; color: rgba(60, 35, 115, 1)">What's changing?</span></strong></p><p><span data-teams="true" id="isPasted">From 12th October 2026, changes will apply to residential electricity and gas prices. Below you'll find a summary of the changes and what they mean for Energia customers.</span></p><p><strong><span style="color: rgba(60, 35, 115, 1)">Energia Price Changes  </span></strong></p><ul><li style="font-size: 18px"><strong>Electricity </strong>customers will see a 4.73% increase to the average annual bill which equates to €1.67 per week. The electricity standing charge will increase by 5% for these customers. </li><li style="font-size: 18px"><strong>Gas </strong>customers will see a 9.38%<strong> </strong>increase to the average annual bill which equates to €2.74 per week. There will be no change to gas standing charges.</li><li style="font-size: 18px"><strong>Dual Fuel </strong>customers will see a 6.73% increase to the average annual bill which equates to €4.41 per week. <span data-teams="true" id="isPasted">The electricity standing charge will increase by 5% for these customers and there will be no change to gas standing charges.</span><strong><br></strong></li></ul><p><a href="/about-energia/our-tariffs" style="font-size: 18px">Full details of changes to our individual rates and specific plans can be found at energia.ie/tariffs</a></p><p><em id="isPasted">Electricity % increase is based on the Estimated Annual Bill (EAB) for Energia’s Standard Electricity Plan and Energia's Smart Data Plan with typical annual electricity consumption of 4,200 kWh. Gas % increase is based on average annual gas consumption of 11,000 kWh. Inclusive of current Carbon Tax and updated PSO Levy effective 1<sup>st</sup> October 2026.</em></p><p><br><strong id="isPasted"><span style="font-size: 30px; color: rgba(60, 35, 115, 1)">Why are prices changing?</span></strong></p><p>We don’t take the decision to increase prices lightly and continue to look for ways to keep costs as low as possible for our customers. </p><p>However, continued volatility in global energy markets combined with increased network charges means we now need to make some changes to our electricity and gas prices, our first increase in gas since 2022. We fully understand that any changes to pricing affects households and encourage customers who are experiencing difficulties to engage with us for support.</p><p><br></p><h2 style="text-align: left"><strong><span style="font-size: 30px">Help, Support & Frequently Asked Questions</span></strong></h2><p><br></p><h3><strong><span style="font-size: 18px">What can I do if I’m finding it hard to pay my bills?</span></strong></h3><p>If you’re having difficulty paying your bills, we’re here to help. </p><p><span data-teams="true">We collaborate with several charitable and support organisations such as St Vincent de Paul, MABS, Alone, and our customer service team are available to speak to any customers experiencing difficulty. </span>We have a range of options available for customers.</p><p><a href="/contact-us">Please contact us if you have any worries about paying your bill.</a>   </p><h3><strong><span style="font-size: 18px">How can I save on my electricity costs?</span></strong></h3><p>Make sure you are on the right plan for your home. You can check your usage using the Energia Insights app to understand where and when you are using the most energy in your home. <span data-teams="true" id="isPasted">Some homes are better suited to Smart time of use tariffs while others will be more suited to 24 hour plans.</span> If you don’t think you are on the right tariff, talk to our team about changing to a different plan.  </p><h3><strong><span style="font-size: 18px">Will my rates change if I am in contract?</span></strong></h3><p id="isPasted">Yes. Our tariff rates are variable and are subject to change. This is included in our terms and conditions. </p><p>If you are currently on a discounted contract, your prices will be increasing from the 12th October 2026. However, your discount will remain the same and will be deducted from the standard rates applicable to your tariff.  </p><p><span data-teams="true" id="isPasted">As a result of these changes, you have a right to terminate your contract within the next 30 days. If you would like to discuss your plan, please call us to discuss the best option for you.</span><!--EndFragment--></p><h3><strong><span style="font-size: 18px">Will I be contacted directly about this price change?</span></strong></h3><p>We will be contacting customers directly by email to inform them of this change. </p>

What are time-of-use tariffs? Benefits of switching to time-of-use tariff Switch to a time-of-use tariff today FAQs: Time-of-Use Tariff Smart Meters July 08 2026 4 min read 5 reasons to switch to a time-of-use tariff If you’re not currently enjoying the financial savings and other benefits of a time-of-use tariff, now is a great time to make the move. Households across Ireland are already reaping the benefits of smart meters through plans that reward them for using electricity at times of lower demand. With a time-of-use tariff, your electricity price changes depending on when you use energy, giving you more control over your bills and helping you make better use of off-peak rates. What are time-of-use tariffs? Time-of-use tariffs are electricity plans that can help you save money by encouraging you to use electricity during off-peak times. Instead of paying the same rates for electricity all day, you pay different rates during day, night and peak periods. This means you can save money by shifting some of your electricity use to cheaper times. At Energia, a time-of-use tariff on a smart meter has the following three time bands: Night (Lowest rate): 11pm - 8am Peak (Highest rate):  5pm - 7pm Day (Moderate rate): 8am-5pm, 7pm-11pm       Benefits of switching to time-of-use tariff There are many advantages of making the switch to a time-of-use tariff. Here are five reasons to consider making the switch. 1. Save money with off-peak rates The top reason for switching to a time-of-use tariff is that it helps you unlock savings on your electricity bills. Day/night/peak plans offer discounted electricity rates at times when there is less demand for electricity. By making simple changes to the way you use electricity, you can easily cut your energy costs. Some of the top ways of achieving this are: Setting appliances for off-peak times: Set your dishwasher, washing machine and other appliances to start their programmes when electricity is cheapest. This will usually mean scheduling them to start when your night rate begins or early in the morning. Batch cooking when electricity is cheaper: Instead of switching on the cooker at peak times when most people are making dinner, batch cook meals when your time-of-use plan offers cheaper electricity price plans . 2. Make EV charging and battery storage more affordable A time-of-use tariff can be especially useful for EV owners and households with battery storage. If you have an electric vehicle, overnight charging can be one of the easiest ways to benefit from cheaper rates. Instead of charging during evening peak hours, you can schedule your EV to charge when electricity demand is lower. At Energia, we also offer discounted EV charging rates between 2am and 6am. 3. Reduce pressure on the electricity grid Switching to a time-of-use tariff does not just benefit your household. It can also help reduce pressure on the wider electricity grid. Electricity demand is usually highest in the early evening, when people return home, cook dinner, use appliances and heat their homes. A time-of-use tariff encourages households to move some usage away from this busy period. When more people shift usage to off-peak times, it can help reduce demand during peak hours, make the grid easier to manage and lower the need for expensive infrastructure upgrades. You can also explore ways to save energy at home in summer , from off-peak appliance use to smarter EV charging. 4. Track and manage your usage Time-of-use tariffs are smart meter plans . This means they give you detailed insights on your electricity use. By tracking your energy usage, you can manage or change how you’re using your electricity. That means no nasty surprises when your bill arrives. Instead, you get detailed insights and the opportunity to take action during your billing cycle. All this data is at your fingertips when you sign up for Energia’s Energy Insights app. You’ll be able to see: Your usage and costs by hour, day, week or month: Check your electricity use over various periods. Easily spot high-usage times and make changes to cut your costs. Track your performance: Set budgets in € for how much you want to spend on electricity. Get at-a-glance graphics showing how you’re doing against your targets. Estimates on energy-guzzling appliances: See which appliances are likely to be using the most energy in your home based on your usage. These insights help you identify appliances that are pushing up your energy bills. You can then change how and when you use them. Comparisons to other households: Track your energy usage against other homes in Ireland. Find out how your electricity use and bills compare to similar households. This can be useful for seeing if you’re doing well or whether there’s room for improvement. Tips on reducing your usage: You’ll find personalised tips and advice on how to cut your electricity usage. These snippets of useful information will guide you towards ways to save on your bills. 5. Support renewable energy Switching to day/night/peak tariffs also has environmental benefits. By shifting your energy use, you're reducing Ireland’s reliance on fossil fuels — and supporting a cleaner grid. Here are a few key ways in which time-of-use tariffs support renewable energy in Ireland: Reducing peak electricity demand: When you move to a time-of-use tariff, you’re helping to ease electricity demand at peak times. This makes it easier to manage demand across the grid. The result is that more of Ireland’s electricity demand can be met using renewable energy instead of fossil fuels. Good for energy bills and good for the environment. With smart meters now in place, Ireland is also moving towards dynamic electricity pricing , where prices can vary more frequently based on real-time renewable generation and grid demand. Maximising solar energy: Many time-of-use plans offer a daytime electricity rate that is cheaper than the peak rate. This encourages electricity use at times when the grid is generating lots of solar power . Make the most of green, sustainable energy provided by the sun during daylight hours. Supporting battery storage: If you have solar panels with battery storage , time-of-use pricing enables you to charge your battery when electricity is less expensive. You can then use your stored battery energy at peak times, when importing from the grid is more expensive. You’ll earn from selling solar power to the grid under our microgeneration scheme. Enjoy financial benefits whether you or someone else uses the cheap solar power you’ve generated. Switch to a time-of-use tariff today Ready to start enjoying all those benefits of a time-of-use tariff? Explore our smart plans and switch to a tariff that helps you find ways to save on your energy bills. Start your switch FAQs: Time-of-Use Tariff What is the time-of-use tariff in Ireland? A time-of-use tariff in Ireland is a smart meter electricity plan where your rate changes depending on whether you use power during day, night or peak hours. What is the cheapest time to use electricity in Ireland? The cheapest time to use electricity in Ireland is usually overnight, often from around 11pm to 8am. Is a time-of-use tariff good for EV owners? Yes, a time-of-use tariff can be useful for EV owners because they can schedule charging during cheaper overnight periods. Energia offers discounted rates between 2am and 6am. What is the cheapest time to run a washing machine? The cheapest time to run a washing machine is usually during your tariff’s off-peak or night-rate period. .gw-launchpad-button {

.gw-launchpad-icon-fill {
  fill: black;
  fill: var(--iconFillColor, var(--iconFillColor));
}

.gw-launchpad-icon-button {
  display: inline-block;
  font-size: 10px;
  height: 3.5em;
  width: 3.5em;
  border-radius: 35px;
  padding: 0.4em;
  margin: 0;
  border: 2px solid var(--transparent);
  background-color: rgba(220, 223, 228, 0.5);
  background-color: var(--iconButtonBackgroundDefaultColor, var(--icon-button-background-default-color));
  /** Mobile icon Buttons
      ---------------------------------------------------------*/
  /** ---- **/
  /** Icon Button Size Three
  ---------------------------------------------------------*/
  /** Mobile Floating Button
      ---------------------------------------------------------*/
  /** Mobile Square Button
      ---------------------------------------------------------*/
  /** Mobile & Launchpad Floating Action Button Colours
      ---------------------------------------------------------*/
}

.gw-launchpad-icon-button--icon {
  color: white;
  background-color: transparent;
  border: 2px solid transparent;
  fill: black;
  fill: var(--toolbarIconButtonFillColor, var(--fontColorDark));
}

.gw-launchpad-icon-button--icon:disabled,
.gw-launchpad-icon-button--icon[disabled] {
  background-color: var(--transparent);
  border-color: var(--transparent);
}

.gw-launchpad-icon-button--icon:visited {
  color: var(--fontColorDark);
  text-decoration: none;
}

.gw-launchpad-icon-button--icon:hover {
  color: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6);
  border: 2px solid transparent;
  border: var(--iconButtonBackgroundDefaultColor, var(--icon-button-border-color));
  background-color: rgba(220, 223, 228, 0.5);
  background-color: var(--iconButtonBackgroundHoverColor, var(--icon-button-background-hover-color));
}

.gw-launchpad-icon-button--icon:hover,
.gw-launchpad-icon-button--icon:focus {
  text-decoration: none;
}

.gw-launchpad-icon-button--icon:active {
  color: var(--fontColorDark, black);
  border: 2px solid transparent;
  border: var(--icon-button-border-color, var(--icon-button-background-hover-color));
  background-color: rgba(220, 223, 228, 0.5);
  background-color: var(--iconButtonBackgroundActiveColor, var(--icon-button-background-active-color));
  background-color: rgba(252, 252, 252, 0.135);
  background-color: var(--iconButtonBackgroundActiveColorNoBackground, var(--icon-button-background-active-color-no-background));
}

.gw-launchpad-icon-button:not(:last-child) {
  margin-right: .25em;
}

.gw-launchpad-icon-button:hover {
  border: 2px solid transparent;
  border: var(--icon-button-border-color, var(--icon-button-background-hover-color));
  background-color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.22);
  background-color: var(--iconButtonBackgroundHoverColor, var(--icon-button-background-hover-color));
}

<script>
    function openAccountsDDL() {
        let ddl = document.querySelector("#account__dropdown-items ul");
        let btn = document.querySelector("#account-dropdown-btn");

        if (ddl) {
            const isOpen = ddl.style.display === "block";
            ddl.style.display = isOpen ? "none" : "block";

            if (btn) {
                btn.setAttribute("aria-expanded", String(!isOpen));
            }

            if (!isOpen) {
                trapFocus(ddl, btn);
            } else {
                releaseFocus();
            }
        }
    }

    function trapFocus(container, triggerBtn) {
        const focusableSelectors = 'a[href], button:not([disabled]), input, select, textarea, [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])';
        const focusableElements = container.querySelectorAll(focusableSelectors);
        const first = focusableElements[0];
        const last = focusableElements[focusableElements.length - 1];

        if (first) first.focus();

        function handleKeyDown(e) {
            if (e.key === 'Escape') {
                openAccountsDDL();
                triggerBtn.focus();
                return;
            }

            if (e.key === 'Tab') {
                if (e.shiftKey) {
                    if (document.activeElement === first) {
                        e.preventDefault();
                        last.focus();
                    }
                } else {
                    if (document.activeElement === last) {
                        e.preventDefault();
                        first.focus();
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        document.addEventListener('keydown', handleKeyDown);

        document._accountMenuHandler = handleKeyDown;
    }

    function releaseFocus() {
        if (document._accountMenuHandler) {
            document.removeEventListener('keydown', document._accountMenuHandler);
            document._accountMenuHandler = null;
        }
    }
</script>

                    <h1 id="banner-header" tabindex="-1" class="news-article-detail__title">5 reasons to switch to a time-of-use tariff</h1>
                    <div class="news-article-detail__lead-text">If you’re not currently enjoying the financial savings and other benefits of a time-of-use tariff, now is a great time to make the move. </div>
                    <div class="news-article-detail__content">

    <div class="fr-view">
        <p>Households across Ireland are already reaping the <a href="/about-energia/latest-news/what-are-the-advantages-of-smart-meters">benefits of smart meters</a> through <a href="/guide-to-smart-meters/best-smart-plans">plans</a> that reward them for using electricity at times of lower demand. With a time-of-use tariff, your electricity price changes depending on when you use energy, giving you more control over your bills and helping you make better use of off-peak rates.</p><h2 id="title1"><strong>What are time-of-use tariffs?</strong></h2><p>Time-of-use tariffs are electricity plans that can help you save money by encouraging you to use electricity during off-peak times. </p><p>Instead of paying the same <a href="/about-energia/our-tariffs">rates for electricity</a> all day, you pay different rates during day, night and peak periods. This means you can save money by shifting some of your electricity use to cheaper times.</p><p>At Energia, a time-of-use tariff on a smart meter has the following three time bands:</p><ul><li>Night (Lowest rate): 11pm - 8am           </li><li>Peak (Highest rate):  5pm - 7pm</li><li>Day (Moderate rate): 8am-5pm, 7pm-11pm  </li></ul><p><span contenteditable="false" draggable="true" class="fr-video fr-deletable fr-fvc fr-dvb fr-draggable"><iframe width="640" height="360" src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/hXFLu9LEJ3A?&wmode=opaque&rel=0" frameborder="0" allowfullscreen="" class="fr-draggable"><span class="fr-mk" style="display: none;"> </span><span class="fr-mk" style="display: none;"> </span><span class="fr-mk" style="display: none;"> </span><span class="fr-mk" style="display: none;"> </span><span class="fr-mk" style="display: none;"> </span></iframe> </span></p><h2 id="title2"><strong>Benefits of switching to time-of-use tariff</strong></h2><p>There are many advantages of making the switch to a time-of-use tariff. Here are five reasons to consider making the switch.</p><h3><span style="font-size: 18px"><strong>1. Save money with off-peak rates</strong></span></h3><p>The top reason for switching to a time-of-use tariff is that it helps you unlock savings on your electricity bills. Day/night/peak plans offer discounted <a href="/about-energia/our-tariffs">electricity rates</a> at times when there is less demand for electricity. By making simple changes to the way you use electricity, you can easily cut your energy costs.</p><p>Some of the top ways of achieving this are:</p><ul><li><strong>Setting appliances for off-peak times: </strong></li></ul><p>Set your dishwasher, washing machine and other appliances to start their programmes when electricity is cheapest. This will usually mean scheduling them to start when your night rate begins or early in the morning.</p><ul><li><strong>Batch cooking when electricity is cheaper: </strong></li></ul><p>Instead of switching on the cooker at peak times when most people are making dinner, batch cook meals when your time-of-use plan offers cheaper <a href="/energy-plans/electricity">electricity price plans</a>.</p><h3><strong><span style="font-size: 18px">2. Make EV charging and battery storage more affordable</span> </strong></h3><p>A time-of-use tariff can be especially useful for EV owners and households with battery storage.</p><p>If you have an electric vehicle, overnight charging can be one of the easiest ways to benefit from cheaper rates. Instead of charging during evening peak hours, you can schedule your EV to charge when electricity demand is lower. At Energia, we also offer discounted <a href="/guide-to-smart-meters/smart-ev">EV charging rates</a> between 2am and 6am.</p><h3><strong>3. </strong><strong>Reduce pressure on the electricity grid</strong></h3><p>Switching to a time-of-use tariff does not just benefit your household. It can also help reduce pressure on the wider electricity grid.</p><p>Electricity demand is usually highest in the early evening, when people return home, cook dinner, use appliances and heat their homes. A time-of-use tariff encourages households to move some usage away from this busy period. When more people shift usage to off-peak times, it can help reduce demand during peak hours, make the grid easier to manage and lower the need for expensive infrastructure upgrades. You can also explore ways to <a href="/about-energia/latest-news/summer-energy-saving-tips">save energy at home in summer</a>, from off-peak appliance use to smarter EV charging.</p><h3><span style="font-size: 18px"><strong>4. Track and manage your usage</strong></span></h3><p>Time-of-use tariffs are <a href="/guide-to-smart-meters/best-smart-plans">smart meter plans</a>. This means they give you detailed insights on your electricity use. By tracking your energy usage, you can manage or change how you’re using your electricity.</p><p>That means no nasty surprises when your bill arrives. Instead, you get detailed insights and the opportunity to take action during your billing cycle.</p><p>All this data is at your fingertips when you sign up for Energia’s <a href="/guide-to-smart-meters/energy-insights">Energy Insights</a> app. You’ll be able to see:</p><ul><li><strong>Your usage and costs by hour, day, week or month: </strong></li></ul><p>Check your electricity use over various periods. Easily spot high-usage times and make changes to cut your costs.</p><ul><li><strong>Track your performance: </strong></li></ul><p>Set budgets in € for how much you want to spend on electricity. Get at-a-glance graphics showing how you’re doing against your targets.</p><ul><li><strong>Estimates on energy-guzzling appliances: </strong></li></ul><p>See which appliances are likely to be using the most energy in your home based on your usage. These insights help you identify appliances that are pushing up your energy bills. You can then change how and when you use them.</p><ul><li><strong>Comparisons to other households: </strong></li></ul><p>Track your energy usage against other homes in Ireland. Find out how your electricity use and bills compare to similar households. This can be useful for seeing if you’re doing well or whether there’s room for improvement.</p><ul><li><strong>Tips on reducing your usage: </strong></li></ul><p>You’ll find personalised tips and advice on how to cut your electricity usage. These snippets of useful information will guide you towards ways to save on your bills. </p><p><img src="/getmedia/1c3e436f-6d8f-4da6-adfe-2890d034dd9c/TOU-blog-image_1.jpg" alt="Man looking at his energy online account using a smart phone" style="width: 800px" class="fr-fic fr-dib" width="850" height="400"></p><h3><span style="font-size: 18px"><strong>5. Support renewable energy</strong></span></h3><p>Switching to day/night/peak tariffs also has environmental benefits. By shifting your energy use, you're reducing Ireland’s reliance on fossil fuels — and supporting a cleaner grid.</p><p>Here are a few key ways in which time-of-use tariffs support renewable energy in Ireland:</p><ul><li><strong>Reducing peak electricity demand: </strong></li></ul><p>When you move to a time-of-use tariff, you’re helping to ease electricity demand at peak times. This makes it easier to manage demand across the grid. The result is that more of Ireland’s electricity demand can be met using renewable energy instead of fossil fuels. Good for energy bills and good for the environment. With smart meters now in place, Ireland is also moving towards<a href="/about-energia/latest-news/everything-you-need-to-know-about-dynamic-electricity-tariffs"> dynamic electricity pricing</a>, where prices can vary more frequently based on real-time renewable generation and grid demand.</p><ul><li><strong>Maximising solar energy: </strong></li></ul><p>Many time-of-use plans offer a daytime electricity rate that is cheaper than the peak rate. This encourages electricity use at times when the grid is generating lots of <a href="/home-upgrades/solar-energy">solar power</a>. Make the most of green, sustainable energy provided by the sun during daylight hours.</p><ul><li><strong>Supporting battery storage: </strong></li></ul><p>If you have solar panels with <a href="/home-upgrades/smart-battery">battery storage</a>, time-of-use pricing enables you to charge your battery when electricity is less expensive. You can then use your stored battery energy at peak times, when importing from the grid is more expensive.</p><p>You’ll earn from selling solar power to the grid under our<a href="/home-upgrades/energia-and-the-microgeneration-scheme"> </a><a href="/home-upgrades/energia-and-the-microgeneration-scheme">microgeneration</a> scheme. Enjoy financial benefits whether you or someone else uses the cheap solar power you’ve generated.</p><p><br></p>

Powering Your EV Journey: A Guide for New Electric Vehicle Owners
Take a look through our guide for your EV journey.
Congratulations on your new electric vehicle (EV)! You've taken an exciting step toward a greener and more sustainable future. As your trusted energy provider, we're here to support you every step of the way. In this comprehensive guide, we'll walk you through the essential next steps you should take after bringing home your electric vehicle. From charging solutions to energy efficiency tips, we've got you covered.
Selecting the Right Charging Solution
One of the first things to consider as a new EV owner is how and where you'll charge your vehicle. Here are some options to explore:
Home Charging:
Install a Level 2 home charger for fast and convenient charging.
A convenient option is to take advantage of government-funded support to install a
free EV home charger
at your residence. Through this scheme, you can receive a grant of up to €300 towards the purchase and
EV car charger installation at home
, making sustainable transportation both accessible and convenient.. Be sure to take into account the below considerations before making the commitment.
Ensure your home electrical system can handle the load and make any necessary upgrades.
Consider time-of-use (TOU) rates for charging during off-peak hours to save on electricity costs.
Public Charging Stations:
Locate nearby public charging stations using apps and websites designed for EV owners.
Familiarise yourself with different charging connector types (e.g., CCS, CHAdeMO, Tesla Superchargers) and their compatibility with your vehicle.
Understanding Charging Speeds
Charging speed is an essential factor to consider, as it affects how quickly you can get back on the road. Three common levels of charging speed are:
Level 1 (120V):
This is the slowest option and is typically used with a standard household outlet. It's convenient for overnight charging but less suitable for daily use.
Level 2 (240V):
Most home charging stations and many public stations are Level 2 chargers. They offer faster charging speeds, making them ideal for daily charging needs.
DC Fast Charging (Level 3):
These high-speed chargers are typically found at public charging stations and can provide a substantial charge in a short amount of time, perfect for longer trips.
Managing Energy Costs
As an EV owner, you'll need to monitor your energy consumption and costs. Here's how you can do that effectively:
Track Energy Usage:
Keep an eye on your energy consumption by using smart meters or energy monitoring apps. This can help you budget and optimise your charging habits.
Explore Rate Plans:
Your energy provider may offer specific EV rate plans, which can provide cost savings for off-peak charging. Investigate your options and choose the plan that suits your needs.
Solar Power Integration:
Consider generating your electricity with solar panels to offset some or all of your charging costs while reducing your carbon footprint.
Maximising Energy Efficiency
Efficiency is key to making the most of your electric vehicle. Here are some tips for increasing your EV's efficiency:
Plan Your Routes:
Use navigation apps that consider your EV's range and factor in charging stops when planning longer trips.
Drive Efficiently:
Accelerate and brake smoothly, and maintain a steady speed to extend your vehicle's range.
Reduce Energy Drain:
Minimize the use of heating and air conditioning, as these can significantly impact your EV's energy consumption.
Maintenance and Care
Electric vehicles generally require less maintenance than traditional gas-powered vehicles, but some care is still necessary:
Tire Maintenance:
Proper tire inflation can improve your vehicle's efficiency and extend its range.
Battery Care:
Follow the manufacturer's recommendations for battery care, such as avoiding extreme temperatures and charging within specified voltage limits.
Regular Inspections:
Schedule periodic check-ups to ensure your EV's components, including the battery, are in good condition.
Environmental Impact
One of the most significant advantages of owning an electric vehicle is its reduced environmental impact. To make the most of this benefit:
Renewable Energy Sources:
Consider using energy from renewable sources to charge your EV, further reducing your carbon footprint.
Vehicle Recycling:
Learn about your EV's end-of-life recycling options to minimize environmental impact when it's time to retire your vehicle.
As a new electric vehicle owner, your journey is just beginning. By selecting the right charging solutions, understanding charging speeds, managing energy costs, maximising energy efficiency, and maintaining your vehicle, you can enjoy a smooth and eco-friendly experience on the road. Our commitment as your energy provider is to support your transition to electric mobility and help you make the most of your new EV. If you have any questions or need assistance along the way, please don't hesitate to reach out. Welcome to a cleaner, greener, and more sustainable future!

<script>
    function openAccountsDDL() {
        let ddl = document.querySelector("#account__dropdown-items ul");
        let btn = document.querySelector("#account-dropdown-btn");

        if (ddl) {
            const isOpen = ddl.style.display === "block";
            ddl.style.display = isOpen ? "none" : "block";

            if (btn) {
                btn.setAttribute("aria-expanded", String(!isOpen));
            }

            if (!isOpen) {
                trapFocus(ddl, btn);
            } else {
                releaseFocus();
            }
        }
    }

    function trapFocus(container, triggerBtn) {
        const focusableSelectors = 'a[href], button:not([disabled]), input, select, textarea, [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])';
        const focusableElements = container.querySelectorAll(focusableSelectors);
        const first = focusableElements[0];
        const last = focusableElements[focusableElements.length - 1];

        if (first) first.focus();

        function handleKeyDown(e) {
            if (e.key === 'Escape') {
                openAccountsDDL();
                triggerBtn.focus();
                return;
            }

            if (e.key === 'Tab') {
                if (e.shiftKey) {
                    if (document.activeElement === first) {
                        e.preventDefault();
                        last.focus();
                    }
                } else {
                    if (document.activeElement === last) {
                        e.preventDefault();
                        first.focus();
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        document.addEventListener('keydown', handleKeyDown);

        document._accountMenuHandler = handleKeyDown;
    }

    function releaseFocus() {
        if (document._accountMenuHandler) {
            document.removeEventListener('keydown', document._accountMenuHandler);
            document._accountMenuHandler = null;
        }
    }
</script>

                    <h1 id="banner-header" tabindex="-1" class="news-article-detail__title">Powering Your EV Journey: A Guide for New Electric Vehicle Owners</h1>
                    <div class="news-article-detail__lead-text">Take a look through our guide for your EV journey.</div>
                    <div class="news-article-detail__content">
                        
                        
    <div>
        







    <div class="fr-view">
        <p>Congratulations on your new electric vehicle (EV)! You've taken an exciting step toward a greener and more sustainable future. As your trusted energy provider, we're here to support you every step of the way. In this comprehensive guide, we'll walk you through the essential next steps you should take after bringing home your electric vehicle. From charging solutions to energy efficiency tips, we've got you covered.</p><h2 id="title1"><strong><span style="color: rgba(142, 68, 173, 1)">Selecting the Right Charging Solution</span></strong></h2><p>One of the first things to consider as a new EV owner is how and where you'll charge your vehicle. Here are some options to explore:</p><h3><span style="color: rgba(142, 68, 173, 1)"><strong>Home Charging:</strong></span></h3><ul><li>Install a Level 2 home charger for fast and convenient charging.</li><li>A convenient option is to take advantage of government-funded support to install a<a href="https://www.energia.ie/dealer-partnerships/free-ev-home-charger-offer"><strong> free EV home charger</strong></a>  at your residence. Through this scheme, you can receive a grant of up to €300 towards the purchase and <a href="https://www.energia.ie/about-energia/latest-news/a-guide-to-ev-charger-installation"><strong>EV car charger installation at home</strong></a>, making sustainable transportation both accessible and convenient.. Be sure to take into account the below considerations before making the commitment.</li><li>Ensure your home electrical system can handle the load and make any necessary upgrades.</li><li>Consider time-of-use (TOU) rates for charging during off-peak hours to save on electricity costs.</li></ul><h3><strong><span style="color: rgba(142, 68, 173, 1)"><strong>Public Charging Stations:</strong></span></strong></h3><ul><li>Locate nearby public charging stations using apps and websites designed for EV owners.</li><li>Familiarise yourself with different charging connector types (e.g., CCS, CHAdeMO, Tesla Superchargers) and their compatibility with your vehicle.</li></ul><h2 id="title2"><strong><span style="color: rgba(142, 68, 173, 1)"><strong>Understanding Charging Speeds</strong></span></strong></h2><p>Charging speed is an essential factor to consider, as it affects how quickly you can get back on the road. Three common levels of charging speed are:</p><ul><li><strong>Level 1 (120V): </strong>This is the slowest option and is typically used with a standard household outlet. It's convenient for overnight charging but less suitable for daily use.</li><li><strong> Level 2 (240V):</strong> Most home charging stations and many public stations are Level 2 chargers. They offer faster charging speeds, making them ideal for daily charging needs.</li><li> <strong>DC Fast Charging (Level 3): </strong>These high-speed chargers are typically found at public charging stations and can provide a substantial charge in a short amount of time, perfect for longer trips.<strong> </strong></li></ul><h2 id="title3"><strong><span style="color: rgba(142, 68, 173, 1)"><strong>Managing Energy Costs</strong></span></strong></h2><p>As an EV owner, you'll need to monitor your energy consumption and costs. Here's how you can do that effectively:</p><ul><li><strong>Track Energy Usage:</strong> Keep an eye on your energy consumption by using smart meters or energy monitoring apps. This can help you budget and optimise your charging habits.</li><li><strong>Explore Rate Plans: </strong>Your energy provider may offer specific EV rate plans, which can provide cost savings for off-peak charging. Investigate your options and choose the plan that suits your needs.</li><li><strong>Solar Power Integration: </strong>Consider generating your electricity with solar panels to offset some or all of your charging costs while reducing your carbon footprint.</li></ul><h2 id="title4"><strong><span style="color: rgba(142, 68, 173, 1)"><strong>Maximising Energy Efficiency</strong></span></strong></h2><p>Efficiency is key to making the most of your electric vehicle. Here are some tips for increasing your EV's efficiency:</p><ul><li><strong>Plan Your Routes:</strong> Use navigation apps that consider your EV's range and factor in charging stops when planning longer trips.</li><li><strong>Drive Efficiently:</strong> Accelerate and brake smoothly, and maintain a steady speed to extend your vehicle's range.</li><li><strong>Reduce Energy Drain: </strong>Minimize the use of heating and air conditioning, as these can significantly impact your EV's energy consumption.</li></ul><h2 id="title5"><strong><span style="color: rgba(142, 68, 173, 1)"><strong>Maintenance and Care</strong></span></strong></h2><p><strong> Electric vehicles generally require less maintenance than traditional gas-powered vehicles, but some care is still necessary: </strong></p><ul><li><strong>Tire Maintenance: </strong>Proper tire inflation can improve your vehicle's efficiency and extend its range.</li><li><strong>Battery Care: </strong>Follow the manufacturer's recommendations for battery care, such as avoiding extreme temperatures and charging within specified voltage limits.</li><li><strong>Regular Inspections: </strong>Schedule periodic check-ups to ensure your EV's components, including the battery, are in good condition.</li></ul><h2 id="title6"><strong><span style="color: rgba(142, 68, 173, 1)"><strong>Environmental Impact</strong></span></strong></h2><p>One of the most significant advantages of owning an electric vehicle is its reduced environmental impact. To make the most of this benefit:</p><ul><li><strong>Renewable Energy Sources: </strong>Consider using energy from renewable sources to charge your EV, further reducing your carbon footprint.</li><li><strong>Vehicle Recycling:</strong> Learn about your EV's end-of-life recycling options to minimize environmental impact when it's time to retire your vehicle.</li></ul><p><br>As a new electric vehicle owner, your journey is just beginning. By selecting the right charging solutions, understanding charging speeds, managing energy costs, maximising energy efficiency, and maintaining your vehicle, you can enjoy a smooth and eco-friendly experience on the road. Our commitment as your energy provider is to support your transition to electric mobility and help you make the most of your new EV. If you have any questions or need assistance along the way, please don't hesitate to reach out. Welcome to a cleaner, greener, and more sustainable future!</p><p><strong> </strong></p>

What is microgeneration?
Microgeneration refers to the generation of electricity from small scale renewable technology such as solar panels.
Think of it as a way to be more self-sufficient!
Solar panels
are generally the most popular choice for micro-generation. In this blog post, we'll dive deeper into what microgeneration is, how it can benefit you, tax exemptions to save you money, and how you can get started with micro-generation.
The benefits of microgeneration
There are several benefits associated with microgeneration.
Energy savings
Microgeneration is like having a little power station right at home.  It’s like growing your own vegetables instead of always buying them from the shop. If you’re eligible for the microgeneration scheme and produce surplus electricity, you will have the option to export this surplus to the grid and receive a payment for it.
Reduced carbon footprint
Microgeneration is also about making a positive impact on the environment. By using renewable energy sources like solar, wind, hydro, or biomass, microgeneration allows individuals to reduce their carbon footprint.
What is the microgeneration scheme?
The microgeneration scheme is a government initiative designed to encourage the generation of renewable energy by households. Under this scheme, individuals can install small-scale renewable energy systems, such as solar panels or hydroelectric systems, to generate electricity or heat for their own use. The microgeneration scheme will allow customers with registered microgeneration installations to sell any excess electricity back to Ireland’s electricity grid in return for the Clean Expert Guarantee (CEG) payment.
Tax exemptions for microgeneration
Individuals who sell their electricity back to the grid in Ireland qualify for tax exemptions. Under the new updated scheme, individuals are eligible for a yearly tax exemption of €400 on the income earned from selling excess electricity.
How does the microgeneration support scheme work?
The microgeneration support scheme supports households and businesses in using renewable energy systems like solar panels and wind turbines. To be eligible for the scheme you must own a microgenerator such as a solar PV system and have an export grid connection. You will also need to complete an NC6 form. Once your form is submitted to ESBN they will notify your energy provider. If you do not have a smart meter at the premises you will need to get one installed by ESB Networks.
If you qualify, you will receive financial support through
grants administered by the Sustainable Energy Authority of Ireland (SEAI)
to help cover installation costs. As mentioned previously, if you produce extra electricity and sell electricity back to the grid, you can receive a payment for it. We currently offer our residential customers a rate of 18.5c per kWh exported to the grid.  Also, regular compliance checks, maintenance, and reporting of energy generation data are necessary to remain eligible for scheme support.
How can I avail of microgeneration?
You can avail of microgeneration in three simple steps.
You must own a microgenerator such as solar PV system and have an export grid connection.
You must notify ESBN that you have installed solar panels by completing the NC6 form. The installer should complete this form on your behalf.
Once the form has been submitted to ESBN, ESBN will send your export usage details to your designated energy provider and payment will show on your electricity bill.
How much can I get for my electricity?
Energia is pleased to offer a rate of 18.5c per kWh to our residential customers. The payment is dependent on the size and type of your microgeneration system, as well as how much surplus electricity you export. You can learn more about
microgeneration rates in Ireland
and how Energia’s export payment works in our dedicated guide.
Export and earn with Energia
Interested in selling electricity back to the grid? With Energia, you can generate your own energy and also reduce the quantity of electricity you import from the electricity grid and lower your carbon footprint. You can also learn more about how Energia supplies
100% green electricity
to homes. Our tailored solution for your solar PV installation can be enhanced with a
smart battery
. With the
smart solar energy bundle
, customers can optimise how they generate, store and use their electricity while reducing reliance on the grid. If you don’t want to sell your excess electricity back to the grid, you can store it in a battery and power your appliances with stored electricity. By partnering with Energia, you gain access to top-notch support and
competitive pricing
.
With our microgeneration plan, you have the opportunity to not only save big, but to also play a pivotal role in driving Ireland’s energy transition. Energia’s commitment to customer satisfaction, combined with our extensive expertise and experience, makes it easy for you to make the right switch.

<script>
    function openAccountsDDL() {
        let ddl = document.querySelector("#account__dropdown-items ul");
        let btn = document.querySelector("#account-dropdown-btn");

        if (ddl) {
            const isOpen = ddl.style.display === "block";
            ddl.style.display = isOpen ? "none" : "block";

            if (btn) {
                btn.setAttribute("aria-expanded", String(!isOpen));
            }

            if (!isOpen) {
                trapFocus(ddl, btn);
            } else {
                releaseFocus();
            }
        }
    }

    function trapFocus(container, triggerBtn) {
        const focusableSelectors = 'a[href], button:not([disabled]), input, select, textarea, [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])';
        const focusableElements = container.querySelectorAll(focusableSelectors);
        const first = focusableElements[0];
        const last = focusableElements[focusableElements.length - 1];

        if (first) first.focus();

        function handleKeyDown(e) {
            if (e.key === 'Escape') {
                openAccountsDDL();
                triggerBtn.focus();
                return;
            }

            if (e.key === 'Tab') {
                if (e.shiftKey) {
                    if (document.activeElement === first) {
                        e.preventDefault();
                        last.focus();
                    }
                } else {
                    if (document.activeElement === last) {
                        e.preventDefault();
                        first.focus();
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        document.addEventListener('keydown', handleKeyDown);

        document._accountMenuHandler = handleKeyDown;
    }

    function releaseFocus() {
        if (document._accountMenuHandler) {
            document.removeEventListener('keydown', document._accountMenuHandler);
            document._accountMenuHandler = null;
        }
    }
</script>

                    <h1 id="banner-header" tabindex="-1" class="news-article-detail__title">What is microgeneration? </h1>
                    <div class="news-article-detail__lead-text">Microgeneration refers to the generation of electricity from small scale renewable technology such as solar panels.</div>
                    <div class="news-article-detail__content">
                        
                        
    <div>
        







    <div class="fr-view">
        <p>Think of it as a way to be more self-sufficient! <a href="/home-upgrades/solar-energy">Solar panels</a> are generally the most popular choice for micro-generation. In this blog post, we'll dive deeper into what microgeneration is, how it can benefit you, tax exemptions to save you money, and how you can get started with micro-generation.</p><h2 id="title1"><span style="color: rgba(142, 68, 173, 1)"><strong>The benefits of microgeneration</strong></span></h2><p>There are several benefits associated with microgeneration.</p><h3><span style="color: rgba(142, 68, 173, 1)"><strong>Energy savings</strong></span></h3><p>Microgeneration is like having a little power station right at home.  It’s like growing your own vegetables instead of always buying them from the shop. If you’re eligible for the microgeneration scheme and produce surplus electricity, you will have the option to export this surplus to the grid and receive a payment for it.</p><h3><span style="color: rgba(142, 68, 173, 1)"><strong>Reduced carbon footprint</strong></span></h3><p>Microgeneration is also about making a positive impact on the environment. By using renewable energy sources like solar, wind, hydro, or biomass, microgeneration allows individuals to reduce their carbon footprint. </p><h2 id="title2"><span style="color: rgba(142, 68, 173, 1)"><strong>What is the microgeneration scheme? </strong></span></h2><p>The microgeneration scheme is a government initiative designed to encourage the generation of renewable energy by households. Under this scheme, individuals can install small-scale renewable energy systems, such as solar panels or hydroelectric systems, to generate electricity or heat for their own use. The microgeneration scheme will allow customers with registered microgeneration installations to sell any excess electricity back to Ireland’s electricity grid in return for the Clean Expert Guarantee (CEG) payment.</p><h3><span style="color: rgba(142, 68, 173, 1)"><strong>Tax exemptions for microgeneration </strong></span></h3><p>Individuals who sell their electricity back to the grid in Ireland qualify for tax exemptions. Under the new updated scheme, individuals are eligible for a yearly tax exemption of €400 on the income earned from selling excess electricity. </p><h3><span style="color: rgba(142, 68, 173, 1)"><strong>How does the microgeneration support scheme work?</strong></span></h3><p>The microgeneration support scheme supports households and businesses in using renewable energy systems like solar panels and wind turbines. To be eligible for the scheme you must own a microgenerator such as a solar PV system and have an export grid connection. You will also need to complete an NC6 form. Once your form is submitted to ESBN they will notify your energy provider. If you do not have a smart meter at the premises you will need to get one installed by ESB Networks.</p><p>If you qualify, you will receive financial support through <a href="/home-upgrades/seai-grants">grants administered by the Sustainable Energy Authority of Ireland (SEAI)</a> to help cover installation costs. As mentioned previously, if you produce extra electricity and sell electricity back to the grid, you can receive a payment for it. We currently offer our residential customers a rate of 18.5c per kWh exported to the grid.  Also, regular compliance checks, maintenance, and reporting of energy generation data are necessary to remain eligible for scheme support.</p><h3><span style="color: rgba(142, 68, 173, 1)"><strong>How can I avail of microgeneration?</strong></span></h3><p>You can avail of microgeneration in three simple steps.</p><ol><li><p>You must own a microgenerator such as solar PV system and have an export grid connection. </p></li><li><p>You must notify ESBN that you have installed solar panels by completing the NC6 form. The installer should complete this form on your behalf.</p></li><li><p>Once the form has been submitted to ESBN, ESBN will send your export usage details to your designated energy provider and payment will show on your electricity bill.</p></li></ol><h2 id="title3"><span style="color: rgba(142, 68, 173, 1)"><strong>How much can I get for my electricity? </strong></span></h2><p>Energia is pleased to offer a rate of 18.5c per kWh to our residential customers. The payment is dependent on the size and type of your microgeneration system, as well as how much surplus electricity you export. You can learn more about <a href="/home-upgrades/energia-and-the-microgeneration-scheme">microgeneration rates in Ireland</a> and how Energia’s export payment works in our dedicated guide.</p><h2 id="title4"><span style="color: rgba(142, 68, 173, 1)"><strong>Export and earn with Energia </strong></span></h2><p>Interested in selling electricity back to the grid? With Energia, you can generate your own energy and also reduce the quantity of electricity you import from the electricity grid and lower your carbon footprint. You can also learn more about how Energia supplies <a href="/about-energia/renewable-electricity">100% green electricity</a> to homes. Our tailored solution for your solar PV installation can be enhanced with a <a href="/home-upgrades/smart-battery">smart battery</a>. With the <a href="/guide-to-smart-meters/smart-solar">smart solar energy bundle</a>, customers can optimise how they generate, store and use their electricity while reducing reliance on the grid. If you don’t want to sell your excess electricity back to the grid, you can store it in a battery and power your appliances with stored electricity. By partnering with Energia, you gain access to top-notch support and <a href="/guide-to-smart-meters/smart-solar">competitive pricing</a><span style="color: rgba(155, 89, 182, 1)">.</span> </p><p>With our microgeneration plan, you have the opportunity to not only save big, but to also play a pivotal role in driving Ireland’s energy transition. Energia’s commitment to customer satisfaction, combined with our extensive expertise and experience, makes it easy for you to make the right switch.</p><h2 id="title5"><strong>Want to learn more? </strong></h2><p>Read the rest of our solar guides!</p><ul><li><a href="/about-energia/latest-news/are-solar-panels-worth-it">Are solar panels worth it?</a></li><li><a href="/about-energia/latest-news/how-long-do-solar-panels-last">How long do solar panels last?</a></li><li><a href="/about-energia/latest-news/how-many-solar-panels">How many solar panels do I need?</a></li><li><a href="/about-energia/latest-news/solar-panel-grant">Solar panel grant</a></li><li><a href="/about-energia/latest-news/solar-panel-installation">The Energia guide to solar panel installation</a></li><li><a href="/about-energia/latest-news/solar-panels-cost">The Energia guide to solar panel costs</a></li><li><a href="/business/about-energia/latest-news/solar-panels-support-scheme-amendments-and-updates-for-energia-commercial-customers">Solar Grants for Business</a></li><li><a href="/about-energia/latest-news/how-does-solar-energy-work">How Do Solar Panels Work? A Simple Guide</a><br> </li></ul>
    </div>

100% Green Electricity from Energia*
*Subject to verification through the CRU’s Green Source Product Verification process.
All Energia household electricity plans are guaranteed 100% green*. We match the electricity used by our household customers over the course of the year with an equivalent amount of electricity generated from renewable sources.
This is achieved through renewable generation and Guarantees of Origin certificates relating to renewable electricity generated in Ireland and Europe.
Why choose Energia green electricity?
100% renewable electricity*
Every Energia household electricity plan is matched with renewable generation on an annual basis.
Independently verified
Our green electricity products are subject to the CRU’s Green Source Product Verification process.
Renewable generation
Energia generates electricity from wind, solar and other sustainable sources across Ireland.
View Electricity Plans
What this means for our customers
Every year, we work out our household customers’ electricity demand from the national grid. We then match this with an equivalent amount of renewable electricity through our wind farms, solar farms, other renewable generators and Guarantees of Origin certificates.
Electricity from renewable and non-renewable sources is combined on the national grid, so it is not possible to determine the exact source of the electricity used in an individual home at a particular time.
Each
Guarantee of Origin
is an electronic document providing proof that a quantity of energy was produced from renewable sources. The renewable generation and Guarantees of Origin supporting Energia’s green electricity products are reflected in its annual Fuel Mix Disclosure and assessed through the CRU’s Green Source Product Verification process.
Learn more about renewable electricity and its benefits
Where does Energia’s renewable electricity come from?
Energia supplies renewable electricity through a combination of renewable generation in Ireland and Guarantees of Origin certificates relating to renewable generation in Ireland and Europe.
How does Energia invest in renewable energy?
Energia Group is a leading developer and operator of renewable energy and is responsible for
approximately 21% of installed wind power capacity
on the island of Ireland. Energia’s growing renewable energy portfolio consists of 15 onshore wind farm sites, which generate over 300 MW of green electricity, and an additional 900 MW through Power Purchase Agreements.
Energia is also continuing to develop a renewable energy portfolio that includes offshore wind energy, solar technology, hydrogen fuel generation, bioenergy plants and
battery storage
projects.
Energia’s fuel mix disclosure
Our annual Fuel Mix Disclosure shows the sources used to match the electricity supplied to Energia customers, together with the associated carbon dioxide emissions. It allows customers to access information about their electricity sources and make informed choices about their supplier.
