FAQs about green electricity
What is the Fuel Mix Disclosure and why is it important?
The Fuel Mix Disclosure is a yearly report that shares the mix of fuels energy suppliers provide to customers. It shows the percentage of demand met by each energy source, as well as its CO₂ impact, allowing customers to understand their energy sources and make informed choices about their supplier. The Single Electricity Market Operator calculates it yearly on behalf of the CRU, and the CRU requires it to appear on bills, promotional material and its website.
What is the Green Source Product Verification process?
The Green Source Product Verification Report is an annual CRU report confirming that a supplier’s green source products are 100% renewable. Suppliers submit the total aggregate demand of customers using green source products to SEMO, together with an independent audit, before the CRU publishes the outcome of the verification process.
What is a Guarantee of Origin certificate?
Each Guarantee of Origin certificate, or GoO, verifies that 1 MWh of energy has been generated from a renewable source such as solar, wind or hydropower. They are included under renewable generation in energy suppliers’ Fuel Mix Disclosures.
How do Guarantee of Origin certificates work and are they regulated?
Guarantees of Origin can be sold between European Economic Area states under EU legislation. Their buying and selling are regulated by the CRU and the Irish and EU markets to support fairness and transparency, ensure the certificates represent verified green energy and prevent double counting. Read through the CRU’s website to see the process for regulating green energy claims
here
.
Am I guaranteed 100% Renewable Electricity at a specific time?
The electricity grid combines renewable and non-renewable electricity, so it is impossible to know whether the electricity used in your home at a particular moment came from wind, solar or another source. Energia instead works out your annual electricity demand from the grid and matches it with an equal amount of renewable energy, as reflected in its yearly Fuel Mix Disclosure and Green Source Product Verification process.
Does Energia supply 100% renewable electricity and how do I know my plan is green?
Energia matches its customers’ electricity demand with 100% renewable generation on an annual basis. All Energia household electricity plans are 100% green and are supported by renewable generation in Ireland and Guarantees of Origin certificates relating to renewable generation in Ireland and Europe.
What does green electricity mean?
Green electricity generally refers to electricity backed by renewable sources such as wind, solar and hydropower. For Energia household plans, customers’ annual electricity demand is matched with an equivalent amount of renewable electricity through renewable generation and Guarantees of Origin, subject to the CRU’s verification process.
How much of Ireland’s electricity comes from renewable sources?
Renewable sources accounted for 40.9% of Ireland’s electricity supply in 2025, based on provisional SEAI estimates. Ireland is working towards a target of generating 80% of its electricity from renewable sources by 2030.
What is renewable electricity?
Renewable electricity is electricity generated from sources that naturally replenish, such as wind, sunlight and water. It is one form of renewable energy, which can also include renewable heating and fuels.

<script>
    function openAccountsDDL() {
        let ddl = document.querySelector("#account__dropdown-items ul");
        let btn = document.querySelector("#account-dropdown-btn");

        if (ddl) {
            const isOpen = ddl.style.display === "block";
            ddl.style.display = isOpen ? "none" : "block";

            if (btn) {
                btn.setAttribute("aria-expanded", String(!isOpen));
            }

            if (!isOpen) {
                trapFocus(ddl, btn);
            } else {
                releaseFocus();
            }
        }
    }

    function trapFocus(container, triggerBtn) {
        const focusableSelectors = 'a[href], button:not([disabled]), input, select, textarea, [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])';
        const focusableElements = container.querySelectorAll(focusableSelectors);
        const first = focusableElements[0];
        const last = focusableElements[focusableElements.length - 1];

        if (first) first.focus();

        function handleKeyDown(e) {
            if (e.key === 'Escape') {
                openAccountsDDL();
                triggerBtn.focus();
                return;
            }

            if (e.key === 'Tab') {
                if (e.shiftKey) {
                    if (document.activeElement === first) {
                        e.preventDefault();
                        last.focus();
                    }
                } else {
                    if (document.activeElement === last) {
                        e.preventDefault();
                        first.focus();
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        document.addEventListener('keydown', handleKeyDown);

        document._accountMenuHandler = handleKeyDown;
    }

    function releaseFocus() {
        if (document._accountMenuHandler) {
            document.removeEventListener('keydown', document._accountMenuHandler);
            document._accountMenuHandler = null;
        }
    }
</script>

        <h2 style="text-align: center"><strong><span style="font-size: 30px"><strong id="isPasted">What this means for our customers</strong></span></strong></h2><p><br></p><p id="isPasted">Every year, we work out our household customers’ electricity demand from the national grid. We then match this with an equivalent amount of renewable electricity through our wind farms, solar farms, other renewable generators and Guarantees of Origin certificates.</p><p>Electricity from renewable and non-renewable sources is combined on the national grid, so it is not possible to determine the exact source of the electricity used in an individual home at a particular time. </p><p>Each <a href="https://www.cru.ie/regulations-policy/energy/fuel-mix-and-guarantees-of-origin">Guarantee of Origin</a> is an electronic document providing proof that a quantity of energy was produced from renewable sources. The renewable generation and Guarantees of Origin supporting Energia’s green electricity products are reflected in its annual Fuel Mix Disclosure and assessed through the CRU’s Green Source Product Verification process.</p><p><br></p><p><img src="/getmedia/292b306b-fa98-48ad-a8a1-3e37575db549/Green_Electricity_Fuel_Mix_Map.png" style="width: 635px" class="fr-fic fr-dib" width="800" height="1200"></p><p style="text-align: center"><br><a href="https://www.energia.ie/about-energia/latest-news/what-is-renewable-electricity-and-what-are-the-benefits"><strong><em>Learn more about renewable electricity and its benefits</em></strong></a></p>
    </div>

Energia’s growing renewable energy portfolio consists of 15 onshore wind farm sites, which generate over 300 MW of green electricity, and an additional 900 MW through Power Purchase Agreements.</p><p>Energia is also continuing to develop a renewable energy portfolio that includes offshore wind energy, solar technology, hydrogen fuel generation, bioenergy plants and <a href="https://www.energia.ie/about-energia/latest-news/solar-panel-batteries">battery storage</a> projects. </p>

                                <p>The Green Source Product Verification Report is an annual CRU report confirming that a supplier’s green source products are 100% renewable. Suppliers submit the total aggregate demand of customers using green source products to SEMO, together with an independent audit, before the CRU publishes the outcome of the verification process.</p>

                                <p>Each Guarantee of Origin certificate, or GoO, verifies that 1 MWh of energy has been generated from a renewable source such as solar, wind or hydropower. They are included under renewable generation in energy suppliers’ Fuel Mix Disclosures.</p>

                                <p>Guarantees of Origin can be sold between European Economic Area states under EU legislation. Their buying and selling are regulated by the CRU and the Irish and EU markets to support fairness and transparency, ensure the certificates represent verified green energy and prevent double counting. Read through the CRU’s website to see the process for regulating green energy claims <a href="https://www.cru.ie/regulations-policy/energy/fuel-mix-and-guarantees-of-origin/" style="color:#0563c1; text-decoration:underline">here</a>.</p>

                                <p>The electricity grid combines renewable and non-renewable electricity, so it is impossible to know whether the electricity used in your home at a particular moment came from wind, solar or another source. Energia instead works out your annual electricity demand from the grid and matches it with an equal amount of renewable energy, as reflected in its yearly Fuel Mix Disclosure and Green Source Product Verification process.</p>

                                <p>Energia matches its customers’ electricity demand with 100% renewable generation on an annual basis. What is Smart Track?
Smart Track
is our new dynamic smart electricity plan, giving you access to half
‑
hourly prices that update based on the wholesale
electricity market. Prices tend to fall when there’s high amount of renewable
energy available, so you could save by using electricity during those greener,
cheaper periods.
It is suited to homes that can shift some usage away from peak
times, especially if you have solar or an EV charger.
How Smart Track works
Everyday the unit rates will be published in your Energia online account for the next 24 hours. You can sign up to receive email or SMS alerts a day in advance of any dynamic rates spiking above a threshold.  It includes:
Standing charge
- covers the cost of your electricity connection.
Base unit rate
- a variable rate you will know in advance.
Dynamic
unit rate
– changes every 30 minutes based on the wholesale electricity price.
You can view our current rates here.
Energia Smart Track Dynamic Tariff
This video shows you how to check your electricity prices as they change every 30 minutes, look ahead to tomorrow’s rates, and plan your usage to avoid higher cost periods.
It also explains how to set up alerts, track your usage, and understand how dynamic pricing appears on your bill so you can make more informed choices.
Benefits
Potentially lower bills
Shift your energy use to cheaper times of the day and pay less for your electricity.
Supports the Energy Transition
Prices are lower when there is more renewable energy supporting a cleaner electricity grid.
Control over costs
Monitor half-hourly prices and adjust your usage to take advantage of the cheapest electricity rates daily.
Key Considerations
Price spikes
If wholesale electricity prices spike, you may be open to sudden price rises.
Uncertainty
Predicting your bill in advance may be difficult due to frequent price changes.
Regular monitoring
To get the most value, you need to track your usage daily. If you use a lot of electricity during the peak (5-7pm), shifting enough usage may be challenging.
To sign up you need:
A smart meter with a CTF score of 4 (see FAQ below)
The ability to track and shift your energy use
An Energia online account
Direct Debit payment set up

Want to know more about Dynamic Tariffs?
If you’re interested in understanding how these new smart meter tariffs work, how prices update every 30 minutes, and how you can make the most of cheaper and greener times on the grid, we’ve put together a clear and easy guide. It walks through the basics, the benefits, and what to think about before getting started.

Dynamic Tariffs FAQs
How do I sign up to a dynamic tariff?
For more information on Dynamic Tariffs, please call our Customer Care team on
0818 405 405
option 3 who will be able to discuss eligibility with you before passing you to our team to discuss setting up a contract.
How are bills calculated on a dynamic tariff?
With a dynamic tariff, your bill is based on two things:
How much electricity you use, and the price of electricity at the exact time you use it.
Prices change every half hour, so your smart meter records your usage in hourly blocks. At the end of the billing period, we will add up each half hour’s usage and multiply it by the price at that time. Using electricity during cheaper times can help lower your costs—but using it during expensive peak times will increase your bill.
How can I budget on a dynamic tariff?
Budgeting on a dynamic tariff is possible, but it just takes a bit more awareness of when and how you use energy. Here are some practical tips to help you stay in control:
Monitor your usage:
Use
Energy Insights
to track your consumption and spot patterns that could be costing you more.
Understand price fluctuations:
Dynamic tariffs follow wholesale energy prices, which change throughout the day. Prices are typically higher during peak hours (like early evenings) and lower overnight or mid-day.
Shift your usage:
Try to run appliances like washing machines, dishwashers, or EV chargers during off-peak hours when prices are lower.
Use smart tech:
Smart thermostats and appliances can be programmed to operate during cheaper times, helping you save without thinking about it.
Build a buffer:
Because prices can spike unexpectedly, it’s wise to
include a small cushion in your monthly budget to cover any surprises
.
By staying informed and adjusting your habits, you can make the most of a dynamic tariff and potentially reduce your energy costs.
How will I be able to plan my usage on a dynamic tariff?
Planning your energy usage on a dynamic tariff is all about timing and awareness. Because prices change throughout the day based on wholesale market rates, you can save by using energy when it's cheaper. Here's how to stay ahead:
Check price forecasts:
You will be provided with daily price updates through your
online account
. Use these to plan when to run appliances.
Use smart technology:
Smart meters
, thermostats, and appliances can help you automate usage during low-cost periods.
Shift flexible tasks:
Activities like laundry, charging devices, or heating water can often be moved to off-peak hours to avoid when prices are higher.
Set reminders or routines:
Create habits around cheaper times e.g. Running the dishwasher after 10 PM or charging your EV overnight.
Review your usage regularly:
Tracking your consumption helps you spot opportunities to adjust and save.
With daily planning, you can take full advantage of lower-cost periods and make a dynamic tariff work for your lifestyle.
What charges will I see on my dynamic tariff bill?
You will be able to see a breakdown of the number of base unit rates used for each billing period, the rate and the total cost. You will also see the total volume of dynamic unit rates used for the billing period and total cost.
Is there a risk of paying more when on a dynamic tariff?
Yes, there is a possibility. Dynamic tariffs reflect wholesale energy prices, which fluctuate throughout the day. While there can be lower prices during off-peak hours, prices can spike during periods of high demand or market volatility.
If you use most of your energy during these peak times, you could end up paying more than you would on other smart plans. However, if you're able to shift your usage to cheaper times, a dynamic tariff could help you save.
Do I need a smart meter for a dynamic tariff?
Yes, Dynamic Tariffs are only available to customers if they have a smart meter with the strongest connection (
CTF
4).
What is a Communications Technically Feasible (CTF) score?
A
CTF
, or Communications Technically Feasible, score is a daily assessment used to determine whether remote communications between a smart meter and
ESB
Networks are reliable enough to support smart services. Your smart meter will have a
CTF
score of between 1 and 4.
What happens if my connectivity (CTF) changes?
If your CTF drops below a 04 while you are on a dynamic tariff, you’ll need to switch to an alternative tariff.
Once we receive the notification from the network, we’ll contact you within 3 days to discuss your options. If we reach you and you’re happy to proceed, we can move you to a new tariff during that call.
If we’re unable to contact you, we’ll follow up by email. If we still don’t hear from you, you’ll be automatically moved to one of our available non-contract tariffs 7 days after our initial contact attempt.
How do I find my CTF score?
Your energy provider will be able to tell you your smart meter's
CTF
score.
Can I opt out of my dynamic tariff if it doesn't suit my lifestyle?
Yes. If a dynamic tariff no longer suits your needs, you can
switch to a different plan
at any time. However, if you leave a dynamic tariff, you won’t be able to switch back to it until the end of your new contract.
How volatile is a dynamic tariff?
Dynamic tariffs can be unpredictable. Prices change every half hour based on the wholesale electricity market, which means they can spike suddenly, especially during peak demand or supply shortages.
This makes them riskier than other
smart plans
, and your bills could go up if you use electricity when prices are high. You’ll need to actively monitor prices and adjust your usage to avoid paying more.
What is the base unit rate made up of?
This is a unit rate that is set and charged for each unit of electricity used. This may be flat or aligned to a time of use (Day, Night, Peak). It is set in advance and does not change day-to-day. It is made up of supply costs, network costs & regulated charges.
The base unit rate will be charged in addition to any dynamic unit rate.
Is there a price cap for a dynamic tariff?
There is a cap on the interval prices (i.e. the half-hourly market price) for Standard Dynamic Price Contracts which shall equal the rate of the Floor Price of the Reliability Option Strike Price as applies to reliability options and difference payments in the SEM.
This is subject to change on a weekly basis and is applicable for the week commencing Sunday. The cap applies to the dynamic element of the unit rate only and does not apply to the base unit rate.
This means there is a price cap / maximum price on the dynamic unit rate which is the Floor Price of the Reliability Option Strike Price and set by SEMO.
You can view the day ahead dynamic wholesale unit rates and current weekly price cap via your
Energy Online account
.
Are there any risks with a dynamic tariff?
Dynamic tariffs can offer savings, but they also come with certain risks that are important to consider:
Price volatility:
Energy prices can change hourly based on market conditions. If you use electricity during peak times, you may pay significantly more compared to other smart plans.
Unpredictable bills:
Because prices fluctuate, your bills can vary depending on when and how much energy you use.
Requires active management:
To benefit from lower rates, you’ll need to monitor price changes and adjust your usage accordingly. This may not suit all lifestyles.
Limited control during emergencies:
If prices spike unexpectedly, due to weather events or market disruptions, you might have little choice but to pay higher rates if you need power urgently.
Drop in connectivity (
CTF
):
If your
CTF
drops below a connectivity level of 04, you will have to move to a different tariff.
Where can I check energy forecasts?
You can also check energy forecasts on EirGrid’s
Smart Grid Dashboard
which shows expected wind generation for the next four days.
Where can I view day ahead prices when Energy Online is not working?
If Energy Online is not working, you can view day‑ahead wholesale electricity prices on
www.semopx.com
, which publishes the official day‑ahead market prices in euro per megawatt-hour (€/MWh).
Why are the base unit rates high when wholesale prices are low?
The base unit rate covers fixed supplier and network costs that don’t fall when wholesale prices drop, since it’s the standard, non‑wholesale‑linked part of the tariff.
Only the dynamic unit rate reflects low wholesale prices, so reductions in the market don’t affect the base rate.
Will I be able to access Energy Insights if I sign up to a dynamic Tariff?
Yes, you will still be able to opt in for
Energy Insights
. However, due to the volatility of pricing we are unable to display or forecast cost for Dynamic Tariff customers. You will still be able to monitor your consumption in the same as you can on our other
Smart plans
.
How do I sign up for high price spike alerts?
You can sign up to receive alerts when the whole sale price of electricity goes above a certain threshold. You can opt into receiving these alerts when signing up to your tariff. If at any point you would like to amend the threshold amount you have set to receive these alerts, you can do so by calling our Customer Care Team on
0818 405 405
.
What happens when wholesale prices are negative?
When wholesale prices are negative, you will still be charged the base unit rate for the specific interval. However, the negative pricing will be factored into the combined amount you pay for the dynamic consumption costs included in your bill.

<script>
    function openAccountsDDL() {
        let ddl = document.querySelector("#account__dropdown-items ul");
        let btn = document.querySelector("#account-dropdown-btn");

        if (ddl) {
            const isOpen = ddl.style.display === "block";
            ddl.style.display = isOpen ? "none" : "block";

            if (btn) {
                btn.setAttribute("aria-expanded", String(!isOpen));
            }

            if (!isOpen) {
                trapFocus(ddl, btn);
            } else {
                releaseFocus();
            }
        }
    }

    function trapFocus(container, triggerBtn) {
        const focusableSelectors = 'a[href], button:not([disabled]), input, select, textarea, [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])';
        const focusableElements = container.querySelectorAll(focusableSelectors);
        const first = focusableElements[0];
        const last = focusableElements[focusableElements.length - 1];

        if (first) first.focus();

        function handleKeyDown(e) {
            if (e.key === 'Escape') {
                openAccountsDDL();
                triggerBtn.focus();
                return;
            }

            if (e.key === 'Tab') {
                if (e.shiftKey) {
                    if (document.activeElement === first) {
                        e.preventDefault();
                        last.focus();
                    }
                } else {
                    if (document.activeElement === last) {
                        e.preventDefault();
                        first.focus();
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        document.addEventListener('keydown', handleKeyDown);

        document._accountMenuHandler = handleKeyDown;
    }

    function releaseFocus() {
        if (document._accountMenuHandler) {
            document.removeEventListener('keydown', document._accountMenuHandler);
            document._accountMenuHandler = null;
        }
    }
</script>

        </div>
        <div class="tabs">
                <div id="tabpanel-a52d0be0ef8424e0b98101ef19ef457a2-0" class="tabs__tabpanel" data-tabpanel="">
                    <div class="accordion">
                            <h3 class="accordion__control__heading">
                                <button id="accordionControl-aac07bf0a86084aacb9a499d24330b990" class="accordion__control" data-click-text="How do I sign up to a dynamic tariff?" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="accordionPanel-aac07bf0a86084aacb9a499d24330b990" data-accordion-control="" data-adobe-accordion-block="Collapsible Panel" data-adobe-accordion-title="How do I sign up to a dynamic tariff?">
                                    <div class="accordion__control__title">How do I sign up to a dynamic tariff?</div>
                                    <div class="accordion__control__icon">
                                       <svg width="26" height="24" viewBox="0 0 26 24" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
                                        <path d="M12.667 0.5C19.4121 0.500166 24.833 5.67395 24.833 12C24.833 18.326 19.4121 23.4998 12.667 23.5C5.92171 23.5 0.5 18.3261 0.5 12C0.5 5.67385 5.92171 0.5 12.667 0.5Z" stroke="#AF195F"></path>

                            </h3>
                            <div id="accordionPanel-aac07bf0a86084aacb9a499d24330b990" class="accordion__panel" role="region" aria-labelledby="accordionControl-aac07bf0a86084aacb9a499d24330b990" hidden="">
                                For more information on Dynamic Tariffs, please call our Customer Care team on <a href="tel:0818 405 405"><u>0818 405 405</u></a> option 3 who will be able to discuss eligibility with you before passing you to our team to discuss setting up a contract.
                            </div>
                            <h3 class="accordion__control__heading">
                                <button id="accordionControl-a62c900ad28e547a79a4f564416ff622c" class="accordion__control" data-click-text="How are bills calculated on a dynamic tariff?" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="accordionPanel-a62c900ad28e547a79a4f564416ff622c" data-accordion-control="" data-adobe-accordion-block="Collapsible Panel" data-adobe-accordion-title="How are bills calculated on a dynamic tariff?">
                                    <div class="accordion__control__title">How are bills calculated on a dynamic tariff?</div>
                                    <div class="accordion__control__icon">
                                       <svg width="26" height="24" viewBox="0 0 26 24" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
                                        <path d="M12.667 0.5C19.4121 0.500166 24.833 5.67395 24.833 12C24.833 18.326 19.4121 23.4998 12.667 23.5C5.92171 23.5 0.5 18.3261 0.5 12C0.5 5.67385 5.92171 0.5 12.667 0.5Z" stroke="#AF195F"></path>
                                        <line class="open" x1="16.8334" y1="12.0092" x2="8.50002" y2="12.0092" stroke="#AF185F" stroke-linecap="round"></line>
                                        <line class="close" x1="12.6483" y1="8.0791" x2="12.6483" y2="15.9212" stroke="#AF185F" stroke-linecap="round"></line>
                                        </svg>
                                    </div>
                                </button>
                            </h3>
                            <div id="accordionPanel-a62c900ad28e547a79a4f564416ff622c" class="accordion__panel" role="region" aria-labelledby="accordionControl-a62c900ad28e547a79a4f564416ff622c" hidden="">
                                <p>With a dynamic tariff, your bill is based on two things:</p>

<p>How much electricity you use, and the price of electricity at the exact time you use it.</p>

<p>Prices change every half hour, so your smart meter records your usage in hourly blocks. At the end of the billing period, we will add up each half hour’s usage and multiply it by the price at that time. Using electricity during cheaper times can help lower your costs—but using it during expensive peak times will increase your bill.</p>

                            </div>
                            <h3 class="accordion__control__heading">
                                <button id="accordionControl-a2d3540776e504b9abff8bffd112a6a76" class="accordion__control" data-click-text="How can I budget on a dynamic tariff?" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="accordionPanel-a2d3540776e504b9abff8bffd112a6a76" data-accordion-control="" data-adobe-accordion-block="Collapsible Panel" data-adobe-accordion-title="How can I budget on a dynamic tariff?">
                                    <div class="accordion__control__title">How can I budget on a dynamic tariff?</div>
                                    <div class="accordion__control__icon">
                                       <svg width="26" height="24" viewBox="0 0 26 24" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
                                        <path d="M12.667 0.5C19.4121 0.500166 24.833 5.67395 24.833 12C24.833 18.326 19.4121 23.4998 12.667 23.5C5.92171 23.5 0.5 18.3261 0.5 12C0.5 5.67385 5.92171 0.5 12.667 0.5Z" stroke="#AF195F"></path>
                                        <line class="open" x1="16.8334" y1="12.0092" x2="8.50002" y2="12.0092" stroke="#AF185F" stroke-linecap="round"></line>
                                        <line class="close" x1="12.6483" y1="8.0791" x2="12.6483" y2="15.9212" stroke="#AF185F" stroke-linecap="round"></line>
                                        </svg>
                                    </div>
                                </button>
                            </h3>
                            <div id="accordionPanel-a2d3540776e504b9abff8bffd112a6a76" class="accordion__panel" role="region" aria-labelledby="accordionControl-a2d3540776e504b9abff8bffd112a6a76" hidden="">
                                <p>Budgeting on a dynamic tariff is possible, but it just takes a bit more awareness of when and how you use energy. Here are some practical tips to help you stay in control:</p>

<p><strong>Monitor your usage:</strong> Use <a href="/guide-to-smart-meters/energy-insights">Energy Insights</a> to track your consumption and spot patterns that could be costing you more.</p>

<p><strong>Understand price fluctuations:</strong> Dynamic tariffs follow wholesale energy prices, which change throughout the day. Prices are typically higher during peak hours (like early evenings) and lower overnight or mid-day.</p>

<p><strong>Shift your usage:</strong> Try to run appliances like washing machines, dishwashers, or EV chargers during off-peak hours when prices are lower.</p>

<p><strong>Use smart tech:</strong> Smart thermostats and appliances can be programmed to operate during cheaper times, helping you save without thinking about it.</p>

<p><strong>Build a buffer:</strong> Because prices can spike unexpectedly, it’s wise to<a href="https://energyonline.energia.ie/fastpay/"> include a small cushion in your monthly budget to cover any surprises</a>.</p>

<p>By staying informed and adjusting your habits, you can make the most of a dynamic tariff and potentially reduce your energy costs.</p>

                            </div>
                            <h3 class="accordion__control__heading">
                                <button id="accordionControl-ab22b51b3fd4c4fc48c809f978b493104" class="accordion__control" data-click-text="How will I be able to plan my usage on a dynamic tariff?" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="accordionPanel-ab22b51b3fd4c4fc48c809f978b493104" data-accordion-control="" data-adobe-accordion-block="Collapsible Panel" data-adobe-accordion-title="How will I be able to plan my usage on a dynamic tariff?">
                                    <div class="accordion__control__title">How will I be able to plan my usage on a dynamic tariff?</div>
                                    <div class="accordion__control__icon">
                                       <svg width="26" height="24" viewBox="0 0 26 24" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
                                        <path d="M12.667 0.5C19.4121 0.500166 24.833 5.67395 24.833 12C24.833 18.326 19.4121 23.4998 12.667 23.5C5.92171 23.5 0.5 18.3261 0.5 12C0.5 5.67385 5.92171 0.5 12.667 0.5Z" stroke="#AF195F"></path>
                                        <line class="open" x1="16.8334" y1="12.0092" x2="8.50002" y2="12.0092" stroke="#AF185F" stroke-linecap="round"></line>
                                        <line class="close" x1="12.6483" y1="8.0791" x2="12.6483" y2="15.9212" stroke="#AF185F" stroke-linecap="round"></line>
                                        </svg>
                                    </div>
                                </button>
                            </h3>
                            <div id="accordionPanel-ab22b51b3fd4c4fc48c809f978b493104" class="accordion__panel" role="region" aria-labelledby="accordionControl-ab22b51b3fd4c4fc48c809f978b493104" hidden="">
                                <p>Planning your energy usage on a dynamic tariff is all about timing and awareness. Because prices change throughout the day based on wholesale market rates, you can save by using energy when it's cheaper. Here's how to stay ahead:</p>

<p><strong>Check price forecasts:</strong> You will be provided with daily price updates through your <a href="https://energyonline.energia.ie/">online account</a>. Use these to plan when to run appliances.</p>

<p><strong>Use smart technology:</strong> <a href="/guide-to-smart-meters">Smart meters</a>, thermostats, and appliances can help you automate usage during low-cost periods.</p>

<p><strong>Shift flexible tasks:</strong> Activities like laundry, charging devices, or heating water can often be moved to off-peak hours to avoid when prices are higher.</p>

<p><strong>Set reminders or routines: </strong>Create habits around cheaper times e.g. Running the dishwasher after 10 PM or charging your EV overnight.</p>

<p><strong>Review your usage regularly:</strong> Tracking your consumption helps you spot opportunities to adjust and save.</p>

<p>With daily planning, you can take full advantage of lower-cost periods and make a dynamic tariff work for your lifestyle.</p>

                            </div>
                            <h3 class="accordion__control__heading">

                                    <div class="accordion__control__title">What charges will I see on my dynamic tariff bill?</div>

                            <div id="accordionPanel-afc44e8eb69404d6ab25e6cfa9fc4772a" class="accordion__panel" role="region" aria-labelledby="accordionControl-afc44e8eb69404d6ab25e6cfa9fc4772a" hidden="">
                                <p>You will be able to see a breakdown of the number of base unit rates used for each billing period, the rate and the total cost. You will also see the total volume of dynamic unit rates used for the billing period and total cost.</p>

                            </div>
                            <h3 class="accordion__control__heading">
                                <button id="accordionControl-a4cff1185ef5541e6add618851cc07ff5" class="accordion__control" data-click-text="Is there a risk of paying more when on a dynamic tariff?" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="accordionPanel-a4cff1185ef5541e6add618851cc07ff5" data-accordion-control="" data-adobe-accordion-block="Collapsible Panel" data-adobe-accordion-title="Is there a risk of paying more when on a dynamic tariff?">
                                    <div class="accordion__control__title">Is there a risk of paying more when on a dynamic tariff?</div>
                                    <div class="accordion__control__icon">
                                       <svg width="26" height="24" viewBox="0 0 26 24" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
                                        <path d="M12.667 0.5C19.4121 0.500166 24.833 5.67395 24.833 12C24.833 18.326 19.4121 23.4998 12.667 23.5C5.92171 23.5 0.5 18.3261 0.5 12C0.5 5.67385 5.92171 0.5 12.667 0.5Z" stroke="#AF195F"></path>
                                        <line class="open" x1="16.8334" y1="12.0092" x2="8.50002" y2="12.0092" stroke="#AF185F" stroke-linecap="round"></line>
                                        <line class="close" x1="12.6483" y1="8.0791" x2="12.6483" y2="15.9212" stroke="#AF185F" stroke-linecap="round"></line>
                                        </svg>
                                    </div>
                                </button>
                            </h3>
                            <div id="accordionPanel-a4cff1185ef5541e6add618851cc07ff5" class="accordion__panel" role="region" aria-labelledby="accordionControl-a4cff1185ef5541e6add618851cc07ff5" hidden="">
                                <p>Yes, there is a possibility. Dynamic tariffs reflect wholesale energy prices, which fluctuate throughout the day. While there can be lower prices during off-peak hours, prices can spike during periods of high demand or market volatility.</p>

<p>If you use most of your energy during these peak times, you could end up paying more than you would on other smart plans. However, if you're able to shift your usage to cheaper times, a dynamic tariff could help you save.</p>

                            </div>
                            <h3 class="accordion__control__heading">
                                <button id="accordionControl-a8225b8f6587940da9c5fc07c015dc82e" class="accordion__control" data-click-text="Do I need a smart meter for a dynamic tariff?" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="accordionPanel-a8225b8f6587940da9c5fc07c015dc82e" data-accordion-control="" data-adobe-accordion-block="Collapsible Panel" data-adobe-accordion-title="Do I need a smart meter for a dynamic tariff?">
                                    <div class="accordion__control__title">Do I need a smart meter for a dynamic tariff?</div>
                                    <div class="accordion__control__icon">
                                       <svg width="26" height="24" viewBox="0 0 26 24" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
                                        <path d="M12.667 0.5C19.4121 0.500166 24.833 5.67395 24.833 12C24.833 18.326 19.4121 23.4998 12.667 23.5C5.92171 23.5 0.5 18.3261 0.5 12C0.5 5.67385 5.92171 0.5 12.667 0.5Z" stroke="#AF195F"></path>

                            </h3>
                            <div id="accordionPanel-a8225b8f6587940da9c5fc07c015dc82e" class="accordion__panel" role="region" aria-labelledby="accordionControl-a8225b8f6587940da9c5fc07c015dc82e" hidden="">
                                <p>Yes, Dynamic Tariffs are only available to customers if they have a smart meter with the strongest connection (<abbr title="Communications Technically Feasible">CTF</abbr> 4).</p>

                            </div>
                            <h3 class="accordion__control__heading">
                                <button id="accordionControl-a5f1d4817715b4dd090e5da09dc2450b6" class="accordion__control" data-click-text="What is a Communications Technically Feasible (CTF) score?" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="accordionPanel-a5f1d4817715b4dd090e5da09dc2450b6" data-accordion-control="" data-adobe-accordion-block="Collapsible Panel" data-adobe-accordion-title="What is a Communications Technically Feasible (CTF) score?">
                                    <div class="accordion__control__title">What is a Communications Technically Feasible (CTF) score?</div>
                                    <div class="accordion__control__icon">
                                       <svg width="26" height="24" viewBox="0 0 26 24" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
                                        <path d="M12.667 0.5C19.4121 0.500166 24.833 5.67395 24.833 12C24.833 18.326 19.4121 23.4998 12.667 23.5C5.92171 23.5 0.5 18.3261 0.5 12C0.5 5.67385 5.92171 0.5 12.667 0.5Z" stroke="#AF195F"></path>
                                        <line class="open" x1="16.8334" y1="12.0092" x2="8.50002" y2="12.0092" stroke="#AF185F" stroke-linecap="round"></line>
                                        <line class="close" x1="12.6483" y1="8.0791" x2="12.6483" y2="15.9212" stroke="#AF185F" stroke-linecap="round"></line>

                                </button>
                            </h3>
                            <div id="accordionPanel-a5f1d4817715b4dd090e5da09dc2450b6" class="accordion__panel" role="region" aria-labelledby="accordionControl-a5f1d4817715b4dd090e5da09dc2450b6" hidden="">
                                <p>A <abbr title="Communications Technically Feasible">CTF</abbr>, or Communications Technically Feasible, score is a daily assessment used to determine whether remote communications between a smart meter and <abbr title="Electricity Supply Board">ESB</abbr> Networks are reliable enough to support smart services. Your smart meter will have a <abbr title="Communications Technically Feasible">CTF</abbr> score of between 1 and 4.</p>

                            </div>
                            <h3 class="accordion__control__heading">
                                <button id="accordionControl-a6518b0fb050f4b5b8d095a05f5bf9e86" class="accordion__control" data-click-text="What happens if my connectivity (CTF) changes?" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="accordionPanel-a6518b0fb050f4b5b8d095a05f5bf9e86" data-accordion-control="" data-adobe-accordion-block="Collapsible Panel" data-adobe-accordion-title="What happens if my connectivity (CTF) changes?">
                                    <div class="accordion__control__title">What happens if my connectivity (CTF) changes?</div>
                                    <div class="accordion__control__icon">
                                       <svg width="26" height="24" viewBox="0 0 26 24" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
                                        <path d="M12.667 0.5C19.4121 0.500166 24.833 5.67395 24.833 12C24.833 18.326 19.4121 23.4998 12.667 23.5C5.92171 23.5 0.5 18.3261 0.5 12C0.5 5.67385 5.92171 0.5 12.667 0.5Z" stroke="#AF195F"></path>
                                        <line class="open" x1="16.8334" y1="12.0092" x2="8.50002" y2="12.0092" stroke="#AF185F" stroke-linecap="round"></line>
                                        <line class="close" x1="12.6483" y1="8.0791" x2="12.6483" y2="15.9212" stroke="#AF185F" stroke-linecap="round"></line>
                                        </svg>
                                    </div>
                                </button>
                            </h3>
                            <div id="accordionPanel-a6518b0fb050f4b5b8d095a05f5bf9e86" class="accordion__panel" role="region" aria-labelledby="accordionControl-a6518b0fb050f4b5b8d095a05f5bf9e86" hidden="">
                                <p>If your CTF drops below a 04 while you are on a dynamic tariff, you’ll need to switch to an alternative tariff.</p>

<p>Once we receive the notification from the network, we’ll contact you within 3 days to discuss your options. If we reach you and you’re happy to proceed, we can move you to a new tariff during that call.</p>

<p>If we’re unable to contact you, we’ll follow up by email. If we still don’t hear from you, you’ll be automatically moved to one of our available non-contract tariffs 7 days after our initial contact attempt.</p>

                            </div>
                            <h3 class="accordion__control__heading">
                                <button id="accordionControl-a356e502d2698475ead98a35cecdc8b77" class="accordion__control" data-click-text="How do I find my CTF score?" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="accordionPanel-a356e502d2698475ead98a35cecdc8b77" data-accordion-control="" data-adobe-accordion-block="Collapsible Panel" data-adobe-accordion-title="How do I find my CTF score?">
                                    <div class="accordion__control__title">How do I find my CTF score?</div>
                                    <div class="accordion__control__icon">
                                       <svg width="26" height="24" viewBox="0 0 26 24" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
                                        <path d="M12.667 0.5C19.4121 0.500166 24.833 5.67395 24.833 12C24.833 18.326 19.4121 23.4998 12.667 23.5C5.92171 23.5 0.5 18.3261 0.5 12C0.5 5.67385 5.92171 0.5 12.667 0.5Z" stroke="#AF195F"></path>

                            </h3>
                            <div id="accordionPanel-a356e502d2698475ead98a35cecdc8b77" class="accordion__panel" role="region" aria-labelledby="accordionControl-a356e502d2698475ead98a35cecdc8b77" hidden="">
                                <p>Your energy provider will be able to tell you your smart meter's <abbr title="Communications Technically Feasible">CTF</abbr> score.</p>

                            </div>
                            <h3 class="accordion__control__heading">
                                <button id="accordionControl-a1833778b51b9451b80153c0369e7fd70" class="accordion__control" data-click-text="Can I opt out of my dynamic tariff if it doesn't suit my lifestyle?" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="accordionPanel-a1833778b51b9451b80153c0369e7fd70" data-accordion-control="" data-adobe-accordion-block="Collapsible Panel" data-adobe-accordion-title="Can I opt out of my dynamic tariff if it doesn't suit my lifestyle?">
                                    <div class="accordion__control__title">Can I opt out of my dynamic tariff if it doesn't suit my lifestyle?</div>
                                    <div class="accordion__control__icon">
                                       <svg width="26" height="24" viewBox="0 0 26 24" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
                                        <path d="M12.667 0.5C19.4121 0.500166 24.833 5.67395 24.833 12C24.833 18.326 19.4121 23.4998 12.667 23.5C5.92171 23.5 0.5 18.3261 0.5 12C0.5 5.67385 5.92171 0.5 12.667 0.5Z" stroke="#AF195F"></path>
                                        <line class="open" x1="16.8334" y1="12.0092" x2="8.50002" y2="12.0092" stroke="#AF185F" stroke-linecap="round"></line>
                                        <line class="close" x1="12.6483" y1="8.0791" x2="12.6483" y2="15.9212" stroke="#AF185F" stroke-linecap="round"></line>
                                        </svg>
                                    </div>
                                </button>
                            </h3>
                            <div id="accordionPanel-a1833778b51b9451b80153c0369e7fd70" class="accordion__panel" role="region" aria-labelledby="accordionControl-a1833778b51b9451b80153c0369e7fd70" hidden="">
                                <p>Yes. If a dynamic tariff no longer suits your needs, you can <a href="https://switchto.energia.ie/">switch to a different plan</a> at any time. However, if you leave a dynamic tariff, you won’t be able to switch back to it until the end of your new contract.</p>

                            </div>
                            <h3 class="accordion__control__heading">
                                <button id="accordionControl-ad5020b73de74446e9bb1b3ef9400a883" class="accordion__control" data-click-text="How volatile is a dynamic tariff?" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="accordionPanel-ad5020b73de74446e9bb1b3ef9400a883" data-accordion-control="" data-adobe-accordion-block="Collapsible Panel" data-adobe-accordion-title="How volatile is a dynamic tariff?">
                                    <div class="accordion__control__title">How volatile is a dynamic tariff?</div>
                                    <div class="accordion__control__icon">
                                       <svg width="26" height="24" viewBox="0 0 26 24" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
                                        <path d="M12.667 0.5C19.4121 0.500166 24.833 5.67395 24.833 12C24.833 18.326 19.4121 23.4998 12.667 23.5C5.92171 23.5 0.5 18.3261 0.5 12C0.5 5.67385 5.92171 0.5 12.667 0.5Z" stroke="#AF195F"></path>
                                        <line class="open" x1="16.8334" y1="12.0092" x2="8.50002" y2="12.0092" stroke="#AF185F" stroke-linecap="round"></line>
                                        <line class="close" x1="12.6483" y1="8.0791" x2="12.6483" y2="15.9212" stroke="#AF185F" stroke-linecap="round"></line>
                                        </svg>
                                    </div>
                                </button>
                            </h3>
                            <div id="accordionPanel-ad5020b73de74446e9bb1b3ef9400a883" class="accordion__panel" role="region" aria-labelledby="accordionControl-ad5020b73de74446e9bb1b3ef9400a883" hidden="">
                                <p>Dynamic tariffs can be unpredictable. Prices change every half hour based on the wholesale electricity market, which means they can spike suddenly, especially during peak demand or supply shortages.<br>
<br>
This makes them riskier than other <a href="/guide-to-smart-meters/best-smart-plans">smart plans</a>, and your bills could go up if you use electricity when prices are high. You’ll need to actively monitor prices and adjust your usage to avoid paying more.</p>

                            </div>
                            <h3 class="accordion__control__heading">
                                <button id="accordionControl-abf3b74183496462588c17715a708464c" class="accordion__control" data-click-text="What is the base unit rate made up of? " aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="accordionPanel-abf3b74183496462588c17715a708464c" data-accordion-control="" data-adobe-accordion-block="Collapsible Panel" data-adobe-accordion-title="What is the base unit rate made up of? ">
                                    <div class="accordion__control__title">What is the base unit rate made up of? </div>
                                    <div class="accordion__control__icon">
                                       <svg width="26" height="24" viewBox="0 0 26 24" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
                                        <path d="M12.667 0.5C19.4121 0.500166 24.833 5.67395 24.833 12C24.833 18.326 19.4121 23.4998 12.667 23.5C5.92171 23.5 0.5 18.3261 0.5 12C0.5 5.67385 5.92171 0.5 12.667 0.5Z" stroke="#AF195F"></path>
                                        <line class="open" x1="16.8334" y1="12.0092" x2="8.50002" y2="12.0092" stroke="#AF185F" stroke-linecap="round"></line>
                                        <line class="close" x1="12.6483" y1="8.0791" x2="12.6483" y2="15.9212" stroke="#AF185F" stroke-linecap="round"></line>
                                        </svg>
                                    </div>
                                </button>
                            </h3>
                            <div id="accordionPanel-abf3b74183496462588c17715a708464c" class="accordion__panel" role="region" aria-labelledby="accordionControl-abf3b74183496462588c17715a708464c" hidden="">
                                <p>This is a unit rate that is set and charged for each unit of electricity used. This may be flat or aligned to a time of use (Day, Night, Peak). It is set in advance and does not change day-to-day. It is made up of supply costs, network costs & regulated charges.</p>

<p>The base unit rate will be charged in addition to any dynamic unit rate.</p>

                            </div>
                            <h3 class="accordion__control__heading">
                                <button id="accordionControl-a9b93870c9c9142ec9c2711a9635f5029" class="accordion__control" data-click-text="Is there a price cap for a dynamic tariff?" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="accordionPanel-a9b93870c9c9142ec9c2711a9635f5029" data-accordion-control="" data-adobe-accordion-block="Collapsible Panel" data-adobe-accordion-title="Is there a price cap for a dynamic tariff?">
                                    <div class="accordion__control__title">Is there a price cap for a dynamic tariff?</div>
                                    <div class="accordion__control__icon">
                                       <svg width="26" height="24" viewBox="0 0 26 24" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
                                        <path d="M12.667 0.5C19.4121 0.500166 24.833 5.67395 24.833 12C24.833 18.326 19.4121 23.4998 12.667 23.5C5.92171 23.5 0.5 18.3261 0.5 12C0.5 5.67385 5.92171 0.5 12.667 0.5Z" stroke="#AF195F"></path>
                                        <line class="open" x1="16.8334" y1="12.0092" x2="8.50002" y2="12.0092" stroke="#AF185F" stroke-linecap="round"></line>
                                        <line class="close" x1="12.6483" y1="8.0791" x2="12.6483" y2="15.9212" stroke="#AF185F" stroke-linecap="round"></line>
                                        </svg>
                                    </div>
                                </button>
                            </h3>
                            <div id="accordionPanel-a9b93870c9c9142ec9c2711a9635f5029" class="accordion__panel" role="region" aria-labelledby="accordionControl-a9b93870c9c9142ec9c2711a9635f5029" hidden="">
                                <p>There is a cap on the interval prices (i.e. the half-hourly market price) for Standard Dynamic Price Contracts which shall equal the rate of the Floor Price of the Reliability Option Strike Price as applies to reliability options and difference payments in the SEM.<br>
<br>
This is subject to change on a weekly basis and is applicable for the week commencing Sunday. The cap applies to the dynamic element of the unit rate only and does not apply to the base unit rate.<br>
<br>
This means there is a price cap / maximum price on the dynamic unit rate which is the Floor Price of the Reliability Option Strike Price and set by SEMO.</p>

<p>You can view the day ahead dynamic wholesale unit rates and current weekly price cap via your <a href="https://energyonline.energia.ie/">Energy Online account</a>.</p>

                            </div>
                            <h3 class="accordion__control__heading">
                                <button id="accordionControl-ac7f7e622bb5240a1b05b40bb2018ff67" class="accordion__control" data-click-text="Are there any risks with a dynamic tariff?" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="accordionPanel-ac7f7e622bb5240a1b05b40bb2018ff67" data-accordion-control="" data-adobe-accordion-block="Collapsible Panel" data-adobe-accordion-title="Are there any risks with a dynamic tariff?">
                                    <div class="accordion__control__title">Are there any risks with a dynamic tariff?</div>
                                    <div class="accordion__control__icon">
                                       <svg width="26" height="24" viewBox="0 0 26 24" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
                                        <path d="M12.667 0.5C19.4121 0.500166 24.833 5.67395 24.833 12C24.833 18.326 19.4121 23.4998 12.667 23.5C5.92171 23.5 0.5 18.3261 0.5 12C0.5 5.67385 5.92171 0.5 12.667 0.5Z" stroke="#AF195F"></path>
                                        <line class="open" x1="16.8334" y1="12.0092" x2="8.50002" y2="12.0092" stroke="#AF185F" stroke-linecap="round"></line>
                                        <line class="close" x1="12.6483" y1="8.0791" x2="12.6483" y2="15.9212" stroke="#AF185F" stroke-linecap="round"></line>
                                        </svg>
                                    </div>
                                </button>
                            </h3>
                            <div id="accordionPanel-ac7f7e622bb5240a1b05b40bb2018ff67" class="accordion__panel" role="region" aria-labelledby="accordionControl-ac7f7e622bb5240a1b05b40bb2018ff67" hidden="">
                                <p>Dynamic tariffs can offer savings, but they also come with certain risks that are important to consider:</p>

<p><strong>Price volatility: </strong>Energy prices can change hourly based on market conditions. If you use electricity during peak times, you may pay significantly more compared to other smart plans.</p>

<p><strong>Unpredictable bills: </strong>Because prices fluctuate, your bills can vary depending on when and how much energy you use.</p>

<p><strong>Requires active management: </strong>To benefit from lower rates, you’ll need to monitor price changes and adjust your usage accordingly. This may not suit all lifestyles.</p>

<p><strong>Limited control during emergencies:</strong> If prices spike unexpectedly, due to weather events or market disruptions, you might have little choice but to pay higher rates if you need power urgently.</p>

<p><strong>Drop in connectivity (<abbr title="Communications Technically Feasible">CTF</abbr>):</strong> If your <abbr title="Communications Technically Feasible">CTF</abbr> drops below a connectivity level of 04, you will have to move to a different tariff.</p>

                            </div>

" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="accordionPanel-a48e005943f6148a2adddfc8d96cc580b" data-accordion-control="" data-adobe-accordion-block="Collapsible Panel" data-adobe-accordion-title="Where can I check energy forecasts? ">

                                    <div class="accordion__control__icon">

                                        <path d="M12.667 0.5C19.4121 0.500166 24.833 5.67395 24.833 12C24.833 18.326 19.4121 23.4998 12.667 23.5C5.92171 23.5 0.5 18.3261 0.5 12C0.5 5.67385 5.92171 0.5 12.667 0.5Z" stroke="#AF195F"></path>

                            </h3>
                            <div id="accordionPanel-a48e005943f6148a2adddfc8d96cc580b" class="accordion__panel" role="region" aria-labelledby="accordionControl-a48e005943f6148a2adddfc8d96cc580b" hidden="">
                                You can also check energy forecasts on EirGrid’s <a href="https://www.smartgriddashboard.com/roi/wind/" id="isPasted" target="_blank">Smart Grid Dashboard</a> which shows expected wind generation for the next four days.

                                The base unit rate covers fixed supplier and network costs that don’t fall when wholesale prices drop, since it’s the standard, non‑wholesale‑linked part of the tariff.<br>

                                <p>You can sign up to receive alerts when the whole sale price of electricity goes above a certain threshold. You can opt into receiving these alerts when signing up to your tariff. If at any point you would like to amend the threshold amount you have set to receive these alerts, you can do so by calling our Customer Care Team on<a href="/customer-care-number"> 0818 405 405</a>.</p>

An Coimisiún um Rialáil Fóntas Commission for Regulation of Utilities
Executive Summary
“Green Source Products” are tariff plans offered by Irish suppliers guaranteeing the source of
electricity to be 100% renewable for any customer on that plan.
Various electricity suppliers in Ireland offer “Green Source Products” to their customers.
However, it could be the case that an energy supplier offers the “Green Source Products”
without directly procuring renewable energy kilowatt hours (kWh). The EU Renewables
Directive and Irish legislation allow the use of Guarantees of Origin (GOs) in the calculation of
annual fuel mix disclosure (FMD) for the purposes of demonstrating to final customers the
share or quantity of energy from renewable sources in an electricity supplier's energy mix and
in the electricity supplied to consumers. As such, suppliers are allowed to purchase green
attributes, i.e., GO certificates, and use them to offset carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions, and
confirm to final Irish customers that the share or quantity of electricity they used came from
renewable sources in Ireland or the European Economic Area (EEA) Member States1.
Irish suppliers with an Annual FMD below 100% renewable fuel sources who offer “Green
Source Products” have the option to go through an annual optional ex-post verification process
called the Green Source Product Verification (GSPV) to confirm whether they have sufficient
green attributes to cover their sale of “Green Source Products”. The Single Electricity Market
Operator (SEMO) are responsible for overseeing FMD in the SEM. They ensure that suppliers
using the GSPV process provide accurate data to justify their green status. The SEMO carries
out this verification process and provides the results to the Commission for Regulation of
Utilities (CRU) each year. After that, the CRU publishes the results of suppliers’ “Green Source
Products” to validate their 100% renewable credibility.
This report covers 2024 as the reporting window remains open for four months after the end
of the calendar year; and there are then a number of administrative steps for SEMO to follow,
the CRU Report is usually published in late October , For 2024 there was a slight delay in the
provision of the relevant data to CRU which has resulted in a slight delay in the production of
this report.
This information paper presents information on the result of the SEMO’s annual verification
process for 2024 of electricity suppliers in Ireland offering “Green Source Products” which did
1 The European Economic Area (EEA) is made up of the Member States in the EU and additionally Norway, Lichtenstein, and
Iceland.
2

not attain an overall 100% renewable annual fuel mix for all their customers’ demand. The
report is best read in conjunction with the more general 2024 Fuel Mix Disclosure (FMD) paper
published by the CRU, linked here:CRU2024159:
In 2024, four suppliers opted in for the GSPV process and were found to have sufficient green
attributes to cover their sale of “Green Source Products”. The report also outlines the Public
Service Obligation (PSO) and non-PSO split for all suppliers’ fuel mix.
Public/ Customer Impact Statement
“Green Source Products” are tariff plans offered by electricity suppliers guaranteeing the
source of electricity to be 100% renewable for any customer on that plan. This report provides
verification of electricity suppliers’ “Green Source Products” offerings for 2024 to certify that a
customer on such an offering was using electricity sourced entirely from renewable generation
in Ireland or other EEA Member States.
All suppliers in Ireland offering “Green Source Products” complete the same robust verification
process to make it straightforward for electricity customers to understand the process and trust
its accuracy. The CRU understands that such a verification process and this subsequent CRU
information paper on suppliers’ “Green Source Products” offerings should provide public
confidence that appropriate oversight of suppliers’ fuel source claims are in place.

1. Introduction
1.1 Commission for Regulation of Utilities
This section summarises the relevant context and background for the Commission for
Regulation of Utilities (CRU) responsibilities with regards to fuel mix and CO2 emissions
information on all bills and promotional materials issued by Irish electricity suppliers to their
electricity customers.
This information paper presents information on the result of the SEMO’s annual verification
process for 2024 of electricity suppliers in Ireland offering “Green Source Products” which
have not attained an overall 100% renewable annual fuel mix for all their customers’ demand
as published in the Fuel Mix Disclosure and CO2 Emissions Report 2024 by CRU.
1.2 Background
In August 2015, the CRU published its decision with regard to the regulation of “Green Source
Products” in the electricity retail market (CER/15/205). This decision set out that any electricity
supplier in Ireland who offer “Green Source Products” must go through an annual ex-post
verification process to confirm whether it has sufficient green attributes, i.e., Guarantees of
Origin (GOs) certificates, to cover its sale of “Green Source Products”. The decision also set
out that this verification process would be administered by Single Electricity Market Operator
(SEMO) and that the CRU would publish an information paper on the outcome of the
verification process.
In CRU18080, the CRU decided that suppliers with an Annual Fuel Mix Disclosure (FMD) of
100% renewable fuel sources do not have to partake in the GSPV process, as suppliers have
already proven (with appropriate checks by SEMO) that 100% of the aggregated electricity
demand of their “green” customers were served by electricity generated from renewable
sources.2
“Green Source Products” are tariff plans offered by Irish suppliers guaranteeing the source of
electricity to be 100% renewable for any customer on that plan. There are two main drivers for
“Green Source Products” leading to the existence of two individual forms:
2 It is for this reason that – for a given FMD disclosure year - the CRU exempts suppliers with a FMD of 100% renewable fuel
sources from the concurrent GSPV verification process.
6
An Coimisiún um Rialáil Fóntas Commission for Regulation of Utilities
1) promoting renewable generation and supporting investment in environmentally
beneficial schemes in European Economic Area (EEA) Member States3 (e.g.,
investment in a specific renewable generation technology or carbon offsets); and
2) ensuring that an Irish customer’s electricity is sourced from renewable generation in
Ireland or the EEA Member States.
It should be noted that the EU Renewables Directive and Irish legislation allow the use of
green attributes, i.e., Guarantees of Origin (GO) certificates, for annual fuel mix for the
purposes of demonstrating to final customers the share or quantity of energy from renewable
sources in an electricity supplier's energy mix and in the electricity supplied to consumers. As
such, suppliers are allowed to purchase green attributes, i.e., GO certificates, and use them
to offset carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions, and confirm to final Irish customers that the share
or quantity of electricity they used came from renewable sources in Ireland or the EEA Member
States.
1.3 Purpose of Paper
This information paper presents information on the result of the CRU’s and SEMO’s annual
verification process for 2024 of any electricity suppliers in Ireland offering “Green Source
Products” which have not attained an overall 100% renewable annual fuel mix for all their
customers’ demand. In addition, it provides the PSO and non-PSO split for suppliers with
100% renewable fuel mix.
• CRU2024159: Information paper on Fuel Mix and CO2 Emissions disclosure 2024.
• CER/15/205: Regulation of Green Source Products in the Electricity Retail Market.
• SEM/11/095: Decision paper on the Fuel Mix Disclosure in the Single Electricity Market.
• CER/11/824: Decision on Supervisory Framework for Administration of Guarantees of
Origin.
1.4 Structure of Paper
This information paper is structured as follows:
3 The European Economic Area (EEA) is made up of the Member States in the EU and additionally Norway, Lichtenstein, and
Iceland.
7
An Coimisiún um Rialáil Fóntas Commission for Regulation of Utilities
• Section 1: Introduction to the context of this information paper.
• Section 2: Sets out the methodology of the GSPV process and presents the results of the
verification process for 2024.
1.5 Obligations Arising from this Paper
As per the CRU decision on the regulation of green source products in the electricity retail
market (CER/15/205), electricity suppliers have to make their GSPV results available on their
website, via their telephone service and in hard copy, if requested. All suppliers who offer
green source products have to provide the following statement on their bills:
“SUPPLIER Z” now offers green source products which is likely to change your fuel mix
when compared to the supplier fuel mix shown. For information on your fuel mix and on
the environmental impact of your electricity supply visit www.SUPPLIER_Z.ie or, for
further details call 00XXX X XXX XXXX.”
Electricity suppliers licensed in Ireland must provide fuel mix information on all bills within two
months of the publication of the SEM FMD and CO2 Emissions Information Paper. The
publication of this information paper also requires suppliers to make their GSPV results
available by the means stated above within two months of the date of publication.
8
An Coimisiún um Rialáil Fóntas Commission for Regulation of Utilities
2. GSPV Process 2024
2.1 Methodology of the GSPV
Electricity suppliers licenced in Ireland who offer “Green Source Products”, however do not
have an annual FMD of 100% renewable fuel sources, should liaise with SEMO who will
advise them of what is required to have their “Green Source Products” verified4. Suppliers
have to provide the following to SEMO:
• A green source submission, which details the total aggregate demand kilowatt hours
(kWh) of all the supplier’s customers who are availing of “Green Source Products”; and
1. An independent audit of the content of the “Green Source Products” submission. It is the
responsibility of the supplier to procure and deliver this independent audit.
From these submissions, SEMO determines and confirms to the supplier the percentage of
their “Green Source Products” demand that has been met from renewable sources in Ireland
or green attributes, i.e., GO certificates5 from the European Economic Area (EEA) Member
States. Additionally, SEMO provides the fuel mix for the supplier’s green and non-green
customers.
It should be noted that suppliers who have proved that their 100% electricity is produced from
renewable sources through the annual Fuel Mix Disclosure (FMD) are exempted from the
Green Source Product Verification (GSPV) process as they have already proved (through
appropriate checks) their “Green” claims. Additionally, it should be noted that where the CRU
has doubts about the reliability of a supplier’s “Green” claim, or its marketing related to “Green
Source Products”, investigation and ultimately, enforcement action may be taken to address
the situation.
2.2 PSO Attribution
The Public Service Obligation (PSO) levy is a government subsidy charged to all electricity
customers in Ireland. It is designed by the Irish Government and currently supports national
policy objectives related to renewable energy and towards achieving a low-carbon economy.
The proceeds of the levy are used to contribute to the additional costs incurred by PSO-

PSO-supported renewable generation must be attributed equally across all customers of the
supplier (irrespective of which customers are on a specific green source product or not). This
is calculated by SEMO by dividing the total amount of PSO supported renewable generation
that the supplier is contracted with by the supplier’s total demand for the period. Suppliers
offering “Green Source Products” are required to allocate PSO supported renewable
generation evenly amongst all of their customers – i.e., all customers of the supplier will
receive the same % of renewable sources associated with PSO renewable generation.
This approach is adopted because all customers pay (and hence contribute) to the support of
PSO renewable generation through the PSO levy. However, the allocation of PSO supported
generation varies from supplier to supplier, as it is dependent upon the number and volume of
